# Embedding the Möbius sum in a sextic family

[Family context](../families/openai-math-003.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Embedding the Möbius sum in a sextic family.** Set $`A_u(D)=\sum\mu(n)\nu(n)\chi_n(u)W(Nn/D)`$ with $`\chi_n`$ the sextic symbol. Rows $`u=p^6`$ are near-copies of the target, so a mean-square bound over $`u`$ controls $`A_1`$. Poisson in $`u`$ produces sextic Gauss sums; the Hasse–Heath-Brown identity absorbs $`\mu`$ into cubic Gauss sums, which are Fourier coefficients of the Kubota–Patterson cubic theta function; its transformation law converts the sextic twist into a quadratic one, where Goldmakher–Louvel’s large sieve has no $`(ML)^{2/3}`$ loss. The general sextic sieve would only give $`D^{7/3}`$. The initial search found no earlier use of cubic metaplectic automorphy to bound Möbius sums.

# Finite rational tests with compactness

[Family context](../families/openai-math-004.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Finite rational tests with compactness.** The construction starts with a recursive theory in which every ring element $`a`$ carries an elliptic point $`T_a\in mE(F_R)`$, $`F=\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)`$, on a fixed rank-one curve. Adjoin $`f(a)=0`$, Skolemize, and feed finite initial segments of the ground constraints to the $`\mathbb{Q}`$-oracle. Dovetail these tests with enumeration of integer tuples: a root ends the enumeration, while failure of a test ends the no-root branch. Each terminating run uses finitely many oracle queries, without a uniform bound. To prove termination, suppose all tests pass; compactness embeds a model in the rational sort of an elementary extension; “elliptic indices” $`\eta:R\to{}^*\mathbb Z`$ are additive and injective; local tests at “contact primes” force $`\tilde a\equiv\eta(a)`$ to high $`q`$-adic precision; a height bound $`h(\tilde A)\ll_f B`$ against $`h(x(\eta(a_j)P))\approx2\hat h(P)\eta(a_j)^2`$ gives $`B^2\ll B`$, so the indices are ordinary integers and the root is integral. This replaces the Diophantine-definition approach (Poonen, Koenigsmann, Mazur–Rubin, Koymans–Pagano). The initial comparison found no matching architecture.

# Five-point height estimate

[Family context](../families/openai-math-004.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Five-point height estimate.** For the source’s fixed five-point set $`\mathcal C`$, fixed exceptional prime set $`S`$, and constants $`H,c>0`$, the bound is $`h(s)\le H\cdot M_S(s)^c`$ for $`s\in\mathbf P^1(\mathbb Q)\setminus\mathcal C`$. Here $`h`$ is logarithmic Weil height, and $`M_S`$ is the squarefree product of primes outside $`S`$ with odd contact order at one of the five fixed branch values of the Shimura curve $`X=\mathrm{Sh}(B_{210})`$, genus 5, modulo its Atkin–Lehner group. Even contact gives an unramified fiber; a sign-obstruction splitting yields an odd 2-adic representation; modularity, Javanpeykar’s bound, Gaudron–Rémond isogeny estimates and Pazuki’s height comparison complete the argument. The statement concerns this specified five-point configuration; no analogue for other branch sets is asserted here. The initial extraction classifies the statement as new and the proof as a combination of established methods.

# Separated-weight interpolation

[Family context](../families/openai-math-017.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Separated-weight interpolation** (Thm 2.1). Fix integers $`m,K\ge1`$ and positive rational $`w_0,v_0,\theta`$ with $`0<\theta<1`$ and
``` math
K\theta^m<1,\qquad K\frac{w_0}{v_0}\theta^m<1.
```
Choose positive rational coordinate weights $`w_1,\ldots,w_m`$ successively above the source’s thresholds; each threshold depends only on the fixed data and previously chosen weights. Put $`W=(w_0,w_1,\ldots,w_m)`$ and $`V=(v_0,w_1/\theta,\ldots,w_m/\theta)`$. At centers $`a_j=(1,c_{j1},\ldots,c_{jm})`$, $`0\le j<K`$, require $`c_{0i},\ldots,c_{K-1,i}`$ to be pairwise distinct for each coordinate $`i`$. Polynomials of $`W`$-degree at most $`H`$ then realize all packets of $`V`$-weight strictly less than $`H`$ under the jets $`Y=1+t`$, $`X_i=c_{ji}+u_i+\log(1+t)`$, for all sufficiently large, sufficiently divisible integers $`H`$. Divisibility depends only on the weights; the lower threshold for $`H`$ may depend on the centers. The proof uses a Roth/Dyson-type curve inequality, nefness on a weighted blow-up, ampleness, Serre vanishing and Rees pushdown. Related interpolation mechanisms occur in Masser 1981, Fischler 2005 and Fischler–Nakamaye 2014.

[Family context](../families/openai-math-017.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

# Surface criterion with fixed-input variation of a rank-two theta tensor

[Family context](../families/openai-math-032.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Surface criterion with fixed-input variation of a rank-two theta tensor.** On a compact ball quotient of SU(V), V a Hermitian 3-space of signature (2,1), Gaussian-completed Taylor coefficients of theta series give holomorphic one-forms and a (2,0)-form $`\Xi_W=\sum\Theta_1\wedge\Theta_2`$. # Deformed critical-exponent surface with BV selection

[Family context](../families/openai-math-074.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Deformed critical-exponent surface with BV selection.** A two-parameter family of critical inequalities balancing a smoothed temporal-deficit cost against a plank-clustering exponent defines $`h(p,z)`$, the least admissible exponent; the theorem is $`h(p,0)=0`$. If it fails, $`h-z`$ is coordinatewise monotone, hence locally BV. BV theory gives approximate differentiability almost everywhere. The source then uses coordinatewise monotonicity to sandwich values at an arbitrary nearby point between comparison values in the density-one set, obtaining ordinary total differentiability almost everywhere; at a differentiability point the partials prescribe the deficit and plank shape of “equality sequences”, and a minimum-delay argument forces a canonical profile and self-similar “stationary packets”. This replaces the sticky/plany/grainy induction on scales of Wang–Zahl. The initial search found no matching construction in the Kakeya literature; the familiar “extremal configuration” heuristic is the ancestor.

# Two-frame entropy transfer of projection theorems

[Family context](../families/openai-math-074.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Two-frame entropy transfer of projection theorems.** Four coordinates of a line refine at rates $`(0,\tau,\ell,1)`$; two marked events give two frames related by an explicit linear map; a robust planar projection lemma (Ren–Wang Furstenberg in shaded form) plus product-slope pinning shows the product of marginals hits the second frame’s support with probability $`\le\delta^\kappa`$ while the true coupling hits with probability 1; data processing gives $`I\ge\kappa\zeta\log D`$, contradicting a chain-rule bound. The initial comparison found no earlier use of this information bound to apply a projection theorem to dependent events.

## Applications

[CS-002: Stationary descent and its information cost](../../case-studies/CS-002-stationary-descent/README.md) adapts the comparison of a joint law with its product marginals through mutual information. # Chart/horizon framework with narrowness trichotomy

[Family context](../families/openai-math-074.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Chart/horizon framework with narrowness trichotomy** (4D). Lines carry one hidden coordinate; a “chart” is a box-times-interval where one quadratic test fits well; the “horizon” is the infimum time cost of true terminal systems; charts normalize and compose. Three regimes (potential/conservative field with “degree restoration”, a Heisenberg-type “horizontal model”, whole-interval localization) each manufacture a cheaper fit, contradicting extremality. This replaces polynomial Wolff axioms: the quality of quadratic fits becomes the variational quantity.

# Holomorphic mass pushed to the boundary

[Family context](../families/openai-math-087.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Holomorphic mass pushed to the boundary.** For a holomorphic map $`f:\mathcal U\subset\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^N`$, $`N\ge d`$, assume that $`f^{-1}(0)=\{0\}`$, its leading homogeneous part has degree $`k\ge1`$ and is nonzero away from zero, and every sublevel $`\{|f|^2\le s\}`$, $`0<s<1`$, is compact in $`\mathcal U`$. The integral of the sum of squared $`d`$-by-$`d`$ Jacobian minors over $`\{|f|^2<1\}`$ is then at least $`(\pi k)^d/d!`$ (the source’s special case of Lelong comparison). Apply to $`f_k=(g(b_1z)^k,\dots)`$ with $`g=F^{-1}`$, substitute $`u_i=\rho_i^{1/k}e^{i\theta_i}`$, let $`k\to\infty`$: Fatou pushes the mass onto boundary samples, giving $`S=\sum_IP_I\ge1`$ where $`P_I`$ is the probability that d independent uniform boundary samples solve all strip constraints. The rescaling that turns Lelong mass into feasibility probabilities had no precedent in the literature examined.

# Latent alphabet gadget

[Family context](../families/openai-math-102.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Latent alphabet gadget** (Lemma 2.1, §2). The construction consists of a binary space $`V\supseteq K=\mathbb{F}_2^\ell`$, a nonlinear map $`C:V\to K`$ with $`C(x+k)=C(x)+k`$, and a rational noise law $`\mu`$ on V with $`\Pr[C(x+a)\ne C(x)]\le p^*`$ for independent uniform $`x\in V`$ and $`a\sim\mu`$, while every subspace of $`V^*`$ with large restricted rank detects $`a\sim\mu`$ with probability $`\ge 1/8`$, the rank threshold depending only on $`p^*`$, fixed before $`\ell`$. It is built from the quadratic block $`Q(x)=(x_2x_3,x_1x_3,x_1x_2)`$ over $`\mathbb{F}_{2^d}`$, update spaces indexed by the $`q^2+q+1`$ lines of $`\mathbb{F}^3`$ (the quadratic term cancels on a line), a trace-duality “alignment equation” $`z\cdot g(z)=\sqrt{z_1z_2z_3}`$ characterizing rank loss, recursive concatenation with a harmonic potential bounding rank loss by 4$`\theta`$ per level. The resulting noise rarely changes the honest evaluation (completeness $`\approx 1`$) yet forces 0.9 of Fourier mass below bounded rank, so the existing degree-two KMS inverse theorem applies unchanged. Barak–Kothari–Steurer 2018 proposed higher-degree tests for exactly this and could not compose them; here degree stays two and the noise changes. The initial search found no matching gadget.

# Finite separation of a shared leg and the shared-leg entropy inequality

[Family context](../families/openai-math-107.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Finite separation of a shared leg and the shared-leg entropy inequality** (Prop. 3.1, Cor. 3.2). Starting with $`A=\sum_hA_h`$ and a shared X-leg, the construction takes $`L=5M`$ copies and substitutes roots of unity. The resulting r-sum is a DFT that retains the terms satisfying $`u-v+2(g-h)=0`$. On these terms, the degeneration weights $`g^2,\ hu-h^2,\ -hv`$ add to $`(g-h)^2`$, so the weight-0 component is the complete direct sum $`\bigoplus_hA_h\otimes B_X(M)`$. For nonzero tensors $`T_i`$ sharing the first space and occupying matched, pairwise disjoint sectors on the other two legs, every spectral point $`\lambda`$ and probability vector $`q`$ satisfy $`\lambda(T)\ge e^{p_XH(q)}\prod\lambda(T_i)^{q_i}`$, where $`T=\sum_iT_i`$ and $`H(q)=-\sum_iq_i\log q_i`$. The construction retains all blocks at a factor-5 cost; Salem–Spencer hashing and laser-method zeroing-out retain at most one block per shared variable. Its ingredients are the Cohn–Umans DFT, Strassen degeneration, and the method of types. The initial literature comparison identified no matching combination.

# Transfer of colorability via Haar rigidity of wild character laws

[Family context](../families/openai-math-158.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Transfer of colorability via Haar rigidity of wild character laws** (§§2–4). Let E be the algebraic plane, K its algebraic unit circle, D the dual of E with discrete topology, $`C\subset D`$ the continuous characters. A K-invariant probability on D is “wild” if it gives C measure zero. The stated theorem is that every wild K-invariant probability is Haar. Its proof combines a Furstenberg–Zimmer compact tower with an explicit approximation property, a transfinite relative-singularity lemma, conditional multiple averages with van der Corput, a radial difference inequality $`w(|A-B|)\le w(A)+w(B)`$, and a number-field general-position lemma. To obtain the coloring consequence, Følner-average any proper coloring over $`E\rtimes K`$; the spectral “wild” part of each color indicator is uncorrelated at all algebraic translations and can be discarded, leaving a measurable “weak” coloring with almost no monochromatic unit pairs. Thus a proper k-coloring exists if and only if a weak measurable k-coloring exists, for every k. The literature since Falconer treats measurable and unrestricted chromatic numbers as possibly different; the claimed transfer equates existence in these two formulations. The initial literature comparison found no matching transfer theorem.

# Triangular polynomial cells with descending precision budgets

[Family context](../families/openai-math-159.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Triangular polynomial cells with descending precision budgets.** A density-increment region is a nested system $`\|b_h-C_h(u,b_{<h})-l_h\|_\infty\le w_h`$, $`h=1,\dots,D`$, where integer blocks of weight h are determined exactly, $`C_h`$ is a weighted-degree polynomial with unbounded coefficients, and $`Q_h=\log(2/w_h)`$ is the precision. The key inequality is that the loss at weight i, $`Q_i'-Q_i`$, is bounded by a polynomial in the precisions at weights above i, never in $`Q_i`$ itself. With D fixed, descending induction keeps all precisions polynomial in $`p=\log(1/\alpha)`$ over O(p) increments, which is exactly a quasipolynomial bound. This replaces increments that reset to a sub-progression and lose a power each round. The trace shows it emerging in Part II as the fix for a compounding-resources recurrence. The initial search found no earlier use of this terminology or architecture.

# Odd cross-intersection parity mechanism

[Family context](../families/openai-math-196.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Odd cross-intersection parity mechanism.** The alphabet consists of the 16513 points of PG(2,128) plus three letters; each vertex of two graphs gets an outgoing label set whose ordinary part is a projective line, arranged so every pair of label sets across the two graphs meets in an odd number of points. Cone off components; $`\alpha`$ and $`\beta`$ are sums of root-component path labels. Stepping both coordinates by a common letter leaves the product element invariant, every vertex of the product graph has odd degree, so every component has even size and every coefficient of $`\alpha\beta`$ vanishes mod 2, “independently of how edges will be matched”. This relaxes Mineyev’s even-product matching and the Rips–Segev non-unique-product requirement to “odd-degree product graph” realized by an oddtown-style design.

# Bounded-pattern estimate for a girth-conditioned random-matching model with prescribed types

[Family context](../families/openai-math-196.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Bounded-pattern estimate for a girth-conditioned random-matching model with prescribed types** (Prop. 3.1): conditional on girth at least $`L`$, the probability that such a system exists is $`o(1)`$ as the admissible graph size tends to infinity: it has at most $`K`$ positive-length paths, total length $`L\le H\le CL`$, at most $`I`$ interval pairs, and at most $`\varepsilon H`$ unpaired occurrences. All paths are cyclically immersed and closed, except possibly one immersed interval starting at a prescribed root. Paired occurrence intervals are disjoint, obey the signed-label matching rules, and traverse distinct underlying undirected edges. The constant $`\varepsilon`$ is fixed before $`K,C,I`$, which remain fixed in the limit. The proof proceeds via multiplicity stages, “nearly aligned blocks” from a simultaneous Dirichlet choice, and a transfer-matrix bound. This reverses the Gromov–Ollivier–Osajda model (fixed graph, random labels) into fixed label types, random graph, with no small-cancellation hypothesis.

# The incidence criterion

[Family context](../families/openai-math-197.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**The incidence criterion** (Thm 3.1): let $`\ell`$ be an odd prime and $`K`$ a finite field of characteristic two containing a primitive $`\ell`$th root of unity. Take a finite hypergraph with $`t`$ points and nonempty blocks, every point on exactly $`\ell+1`$ blocks, and bipartite incidence graph of girth at least 12, together with vectors $`x_v\in K^m`$ with $`\sum_{v\in f}x_vx_v^\mathsf{T}=0`$ per block and $`\sum_vx_vx_v^\mathsf{T}=-I_m`$, with $`0<m<t\le m\ell^2`$; these data yield the counterexample. The key identity uses the fact that $`\ell+1`$ is the number of lines through the origin of $`\mathbb{F}_\ell^2`$, so local copies of $`\mathbb{F}_\ell^2`$ glue along the blocks, and $`\sum_{u\in K_v}u=1+\sum_{f\ni v}(\sum_{u\in L_f}u-1)`$ turns the two identities into $`UT=I_m`$ after averaging. This gives a local-to-global certificate for failure of direct finiteness; the closest relative is Dykema–Heister–Juschenko’s universal left-invertible-element groups, which encode cancellation patterns but give no such criterion.

# Recursive Hilbert-ball-valued coloring of dyadic partitions

[Family context](../families/openai-math-248.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Recursive Hilbert-ball-valued coloring of dyadic partitions.** For a dyadic partition T of $`[0,1]`$, define $`p(T)=f\big(\tfrac1D\sum_jp(T_{I_j})\big)`$ when T respects D fixed internal basic dyadic intervals with strictly positive pairwise gaps, and define it to be 0 otherwise. Here $`T_{I_j}`$ is the normalized restriction. The recursion is well founded because restriction decreases the number of cells. Applied to the image partitions $`gT^{(n)}`$, it produces colors $`X_I(g)`$ for which the parent color equals f applied to the mean of the descendant colors. Moore’s 2013 reformulation uses finite, nonrecursive tree colorings. The initial comparison found no earlier version of this recursive rule with a fixed-point-free f.

# Benyamini–Sternfeld displacement map as an amenability obstruction

[Family context](../families/openai-math-248.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Benyamini–Sternfeld displacement map as an amenability obstruction.** Let $`f`$ be an $`L`$-Lipschitz self-map of a Hilbert unit ball with $`\|f(x)-x\|\ge\delta>0`$ everywhere (Benyamini–Sternfeld 1983; the source constructs $`\delta=1/2`$ on $`L^2([0,1];\mathbb R^2)`$). For each $`g`$ in the nonempty finite averaging set $`A\subset F`$, the recursive identities give the pointwise estimate
``` math
\delta^2\le\|m(g)-f(m(g))\|^2
 \le\frac{L^2}{D}\sum_{i=1}^D\|z_i(g)-m(g)\|^2.
```
The correlation comparisons control the finite averages, not each summand pointwise. With $`\mathbb E_A`$ denoting uniform averaging over $`g\in A`$ and $`\eta`$ the maximum normalized translation defect for the selected transports,
``` math
\begin{aligned}
 \delta^2&\le\frac{L^2}{D}\sum_{i=1}^D\mathbb E_A\|z_i-m\|^2\\
 &\le L^2\left(\frac4D+4\left(1-\frac1D\right)\eta\right).
\end{aligned}
```
Choosing $`D>4L^2/\delta^2`$ gives a positive lower bound on $`\eta`$, contradicting the Følner criterion. The map is non-affine and $`F`$ does not act on it; the initial extraction found no earlier use of this displacement theorem for this amenability problem.

# Small cocycle with a prescribed word value

[Family context](../families/openai-math-287.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Small cocycle with a prescribed word value** (Lemma 4.1). Let $`\Gamma=\mathbb{F}_n`$, and place the coefficient h on the first generator only. The Fox cocycle of $`w_m=(ab_1)(ab_2)\cdots(ab_m)a`$, where $`b_j=x_2^jx_3x_2^{-j}`$, is $`T_mh`$ with $`T_m=1+\sum\lambda(p_j)`$ and freely generating $`p_j`$. Since $`T_mT_m^*/m`$ converges to free Poisson(1), which has no atom at 0, a cutoff inverse supplies h with $`\|h\|_2\le(dm)^{-1/2}`$ before finite-support approximation, where $`d>0`$ is a fixed spectral cutoff, and small $`\|T_mh-\delta_e\|_2`$. The spectral cutoff controls the discarded mass; the absence of an atom at zero does not supply a uniformly bounded inverse. The associated flow changes each generator by $`O(\|h\|)`$ while changing the long word by a full unitary factor. Fox calculus and the free Poisson law are classical; the initial extraction identified their use to obtain this displacement as the new feature. The repository’s Lean development uses a combinatorial partial inverse and also treats $`n=2`$, beyond the paper’s argument.

# Tame variables, finite models and residual concentration

[Family context](../families/openai-math-002.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Tame variables, finite models and residual concentration** (§§3–4). The coefficient ring is $`\mathbb Z_p[[t,u_1,\dots,u_m]]`$ where t is the cyclotomic or anticyclotomic variable and each $`u_j`$ is a nonprincipal-ultrafilter limit of cyclic p-power characters at auxiliary primes $`r\to1`$ p-adically. Nekovář-style Selmer complexes are replaced by bounded finite free cochain models whose matrices have ultrafilter limits, keeping cup products, duality and homotopies. “Residual concentration” adjoins tame directions until one-sided determinants are nonzero mod (p,t), using a first-order lift test with Chebotarev-chosen commutators. This is where Eisenstein and small-image primes are absorbed. This extends Taylor–Wiles–Kisin auxiliary primes and Scholze–Manning ultrapatching; the combination (ultralimits of tame characters as formal Iwasawa variables, later specialized to zero) had no precedent in the literature examined.

[Family context](../families/openai-math-010.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Marked lines and transverse charts** (§§5–6). After a solvable totally real base change through abelian 2-extensions with 2 split and a bounded number of bad primes, record an invariant ordinary line only at the $`m=[F:A]`$ dyadic places over one place of A, with $`m/d\to0`$. This replaces Skinner–Wiles and Pan’s ordinary covering, which records a line at all p-adic places. The proposed new step is to mark a vanishing fraction of places to obtain connectedness, while leaving the propagation step unrestricted at 2.

# Marked Chow relation from Quot-scheme localization

[Family context](../families/openai-math-040.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Marked Chow relation from Quot-scheme localization** (Thm chow-relation). On the Quot scheme of rank-0 quotients of $`L_1\oplus L_2`$ with fixed determinant, $`\mathbb G_m`$ acts with weights $`\pm1`$. The class $`\Xi(t)=q_*(h^p\,ch_2(Q)_{(1)}ch_2(Q)_{(2)}\cap[B]^{vir}\times[X\times X])`$ has equivariant codimension $`p+4-v`$; if $`v>p+2`$ its codimension-2 part would carry a negative power of t, impossible for a non-localized class, so it vanishes. Graber–Pandharipande localization rewrites the same class as a sum over fixed loci $`|T|\times|H|\times X^{[n_1]}\times X^{[n_2]}`$, yielding $`\sum_WC_W=0`$ in $`CH^2(X\times X)_{\mathbb Q}`$ with each $`C_W=c_W[\Delta_X]+`$ external products. This supplies Bloch–Srinivas decompositions needing no family, covering or automorphism. Positive-dimensional localization relations are standard (Faber–Pandharipande; Marian–Oprea–Pandharipande used this exact setup for Lehn’s conjecture); the initial search found no earlier use of this approach for Bloch’s conjecture.

# Supported rational descent

[Family context](../families/openai-math-193.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Supported rational descent** (Thm 3.1): let $`A`$ be a commutative Noetherian $`\mathbb Z_{(p)}`$-algebra of finite Krull dimension, $`J\subset A`$ an ideal containing $`p`$, and $`H`$ a connective associative $`A`$-algebra with central $`A`$-action. Let $`T`$ be a finite commutative $`A`$-algebra with a finite group $`G`$ acting over $`A`$, such that $`\operatorname{Spec}T\to\operatorname{Spec}A`$ is surjective and $`G`$ is transitive on each geometric fiber. The claimed equivalence is $`K^J(H)_{\mathbb Q}\simeq(K^J(H\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}T)_{\mathbb Q})^{hG}`$. In the proof, the fiber of rationalized K-theory under inverting p is truncating because Goodwillie’s HN terms cancel, hence a cdh sheaf; finite-flat descent by rational transfers; flattening by blow-up; a “geometric orbit argument” computes invariants. Combination: Voevodsky’s h-topology and Suslin–Voevodsky’s pseudo-Galois covering lemma (uncited) transported to spectrum-valued truncating invariants with noncommutative coefficients.

# Noisy-observation conditioning with a dimension-free tilt cost

[Family context](../families/openai-math-263.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Noisy-observation conditioning with a dimension-free tilt cost** (Lemmas 5.1–5.2). Observe every electron position with independent smooth noise of width $`\ell_j=r_j^{1.01}`$ at dyadic scales, forget labels, obtaining decreasing $`\sigma`$-fields. For a normalized eigenstate $`\Psi`$ and an observation event $`A\in\mathcal F_j`$ of probability $`p>0`$, put $`p_A(x)=\Pr(A\mid x)`$. With the stated noise law and $`\sum_{h\ge j}\ell_h^{-2}\le C_\ell\ell_j^{-2}`$, the vector $`\Psi_A=\sqrt{p_A/p}\,\Psi`$ is antisymmetric, in the form domain, has the conditional law, and $`q[\Psi_A]\le e_\Psi+C\ell_j^{-2}\log^5(e/p)`$, with no factor of n or of the number of arrays. The proof uses a score bound, Rademacher symmetrization and the eigenstate multiplier identity. Any failure of a local Thomas–Fermi comparison becomes a legitimate low-energy state. This replaces the deterministic Hartree–Fock density unavailable for correlated states. The initial comparison found no matching construction in the examined work of Lieb, LSST, Fefferman–Seco, SSS, Solovej, Nam or Lewin.

# Coupled purity bootstrap

[Family context](../families/openai-math-268.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Coupled purity bootstrap** (Prop 4.4). Two purities of one partition function $`Z_n(b)`$ are the Gibbs purity $`T(n,b)=Z_n(2b)/Z_n(b)^2`$ and the spatial purity $`S(n,b)=Z_{2n}(b)/Z_n(b)^2`$, formed from the spatial-transfer eigenvalues. If a probability vector has purity $`P`$, its normalized square has purity $`P'`$ satisfying
``` math
1-P'\le\frac{(1-P)^2}{2P^2}.
```
This gives quadratic improvement in a high-purity regime, not convergence to purity one from arbitrary initial data (a uniform probability vector is unchanged). Squaring Gibbs weights doubles $`b`$; squaring spatial weights doubles $`n`$. The exact coupling identities remain
``` math
S(n,2b)=\frac{S(n,b)^2T(2n,b)}{T(n,b)^2},\qquad
 T(4n,b)=\frac{T(2n,b)^2S(2n,2b)}{S(2n,b)^2}.
```
The source’s quantitative bootstrap assumes even $`n_0\ge4`$, $`b_0>0`$, $`0<u_0<1/6`$, and constants $`C,r`$ such that
``` math
\begin{gathered}
 G(u_0)\le C,\quad r=Cu_0<1,\quad C(1-3u_0)>3,\\
 G(u)=\tfrac12\bigl((1-u)^{-1}+(1-u)^{-2}+(1-u)^{-3}\bigr)^2,\\
 S(n_0,b_0)\ge1-u_0,\qquad T(2n_0,b_0)\ge1-u_0.
\end{gathered}
```
Together with the transfer representation, these hypotheses give dyadic defect decay and interpolation to intermediate even lengths. The inequality $`T(L,b)>1/2`$ alone forces ground-state uniqueness: two ground states would have equal maximal Gibbs weights. The uniform gap $`\gamma_L>\log(1/r)/b_0`$ uses the quantitative decay and temperature bounds as well. The criterion uses no local ground-state projections; its novelty judgment concerns this gap mechanism, not the elementary purity identity alone.

# Restriction bound independent of clause count

[Family context](../families/openai-math-112.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Restriction bound independent of clause count** (Lemma 3.1). A width-k CNF H under a p-random restriction has the expansion $`H|_\rho=K+K\sum_j(-1)^j\sum_{\text{paths}}\prod v_{i_h}/\prod a_{U_h}`$. Here K conjoins the initially easy clauses ($`\le b`$ live variables), each path records successive hard clauses, and the denominators count violated easy clauses. A marker-mixture identity expresses each path term as a nonnegative weight times the expectation of a width-b CNF: randomly order clauses and markers, then retain the clauses preceding the first marker. The resulting correlation estimate is $`|E[G\cdot H|_\rho]|\le W\cdot\mathrm{corr}_b(G)`$ with $`E[W]\le1/(1-\theta)`$. The Poisson-type tail $`\theta`$ is $`<`$ 1 for any constant pk when b $`\gg`$ pk. Classical Håstad switching has a useful decay estimate when $`pk<1/5`$; the scale $`p\approx1/k`$ with $`k\approx\log S`$ leads to the $`\sqrt{n}`$ exponent. In the signed expansion, normalization averages over eligible violated clause indices and cancels their count. The initial extraction classifies this mechanism as new. Tal’s $`L^{1}`$ switching lemma and small-restriction switching lemmas have different conclusions.

# Slice language

[Family context](../families/openai-math-112.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Slice language** (Def 5.1). The input contains data x, Toeplitz hash bits, a monic polynomial, and t field elements. Acceptance requires the degree-zero coefficient of the polynomial evaluated at the hash to vanish in the quotient-ring representation. In the proof, an irreducible modulus is selected and the hash is required to be injective on the restricted data cube. Random independent field coefficients then give $`t`$-wise independent signs on that cube. Averaging subsequently fixes one setting of all non-data bits with a small failure probability over restrictions; a fixed deterministic slice is not itself a random $`t`$-wise independent family. The construction combines Krawczyk hashing, Alon–Babai–Itai limited independence, and the evaluator approach of Paturi–Saks–Zane. On the good random restrictions with $`m`$ surviving data bits, its correlation with every width-$`b`$ CNF is at most $`2^{-m/8}`$; the exponent $`1/8`$ is independent of fixed $`b`$, while the sufficiently large length threshold may depend on $`b`$. Parity lacks this property, so the argument is consistent with the tight parity bound.

# Seed ball plus fixed-frame completion via a U(2) polar-factor cover

[Family context](../families/openai-math-266.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Seed ball plus fixed-frame completion via a U(2) polar-factor cover** (§§2–3). Dephase H; cover the nine phases of rows and columns 0–1 by 249,878 balls of radius 0.032 after a minimum-circular-gap normalization; inside a ball write H in 2+4 blocks, the kernels of the $`2\times4`$ blocks are 2-dimensional, the compressed unknown $`Y=K_C^*DK_B`$ is $`2\times2`$ with $`\mathrm{tr}(6I-Y^*Y)<0.32`$, hence within p of $`\sqrt{6}`$ times a unitary $`V \in U(2)`$; an Euler-angle box cover of U(2) with uniform Taylor bounds yields necessary tests. Every order-6 complex Hadamard matrix is represented by 13 parameters with no family assumption, giving a finite cover of the unclassified 25-phase continuum. Jaming–Matolcsi–Móra proposed discretizing all 25 phases without completing that computation in the work compared by the initial extraction. This proves that all finite multioverlaps concentrate given the auxiliary hierarchy, the “factorization” Panchenko 2016 called missing. # Backward intertwiner over an ergodic base

[Family context](../families/openai-math-293.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Backward intertwiner over an ergodic base.** $`S=\int^\oplus S_x`$ over the 2-adic integers with Haar measure and the odometer $`x\mapsto x+1`$; each fiber a unicellular bilateral weighted shift with quadratic log-weights plus residue corrections so the cocycle drift has opposite signs at the two ends. V sends $`e_j`$ at x to $`b_j(x)e_{j-1}`$ at x+1, where b solves a commuting-square recurrence, normalized per fiber by a supremum finite a.e. by Borel–Cantelli but not integrable. Multipliers $`L^\infty(\mathbb Z_2)\subset\{S\}'`$ force any hyperinvariant subspace to be a measurable field of tails $`K_{\ge s(x)}`$; $`V\in\{S\}'`$ gives $`s(x+1)\le s(x)-1`$, impossible on a probability space. This extends Atzmon–Sodin’s completely indecomposable shifts by transport between fibers. New as a construction; the Bishop-operator literature works in one fiber on invariant, not hyperinvariant, subspaces.

# Selective bridge via reduced HNN adjunction along peaking sequences

[Family context](../families/openai-math-297.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Selective bridge via reduced HNN adjunction along peaking sequences** (Thm 4.1). A decreasing projection sequence “peaks to” a state h if h is the only state with value 1 on all of them. Let $`A`$ be a unital $`C^*`$-algebra with a faithful tracial state and no finite-dimensional irreducible representations. For two inequivalent pure states, take decreasing peaking projection sequences starting at $`1`$, with equal traces $`1=t_0>t_1>\cdots>0`$ tending to zero. The source adjoins an intertwiner carrying one sequence onto the other via Ueda’s reduced HNN extension (a corner of an amalgamated free product). The claim is that every old pure state extends uniquely, lifts are pure, and the only new equivalence is between the two chosen classes; simplicity and a faithful trace-preserving expectation are preserved. The proof uses norm decay on reduced words via excision, cross-excision, trace-null supports and “moving the peak through the stable letter”. This replaces Akemann–Weaver’s crossed product by a Kishimoto–Ozawa–Sakai automorphism of the whole algebra, which forced separability at each stage and hence $`\aleph_{1}`$ and diamond. Calderón–Farah’s Question 8.1 asked for exactly such a partial crossed product. The initial extraction classifies this as a combination; a detailed comparison with Tanaka’s construction remains necessary.

# Ordered density comparison

[Family context](../families/openai-math-325.md) · [Instrument index](../../tables/instruments.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Extracted mathematical content

**Ordered density comparison** (direct paper Thm 3.2, main Lemma 5.1). For a finite matrix $`A`$ and a matrix polynomial $`F`$ normalized to have boundary supremum norm one on an enclosing analytic convex domain, choose a unit top singular pair $`F[A]x=\gamma y`$ (the zero case is immediate). Compress the Crouzeix–Palencia positive field $`R+R^*\succeq0`$ by $`[X\ Y]`$ into a $`2\times2`$ block $`\Delta`$($`\lambda`$) of $`m\times m`$ boundary functions whose entries have Faber coefficients $`P_k=X^*b_k(A)X`$, $`M_k=Y^*b_k(A)X`$. For PSD $`\Delta`$, $`\mathrm{tr}(\Delta J\Delta J)\ge0`$ gives $`2|M+L^*|^2_{HS}\le|P+P^*|^2_{HS}+|Q+Q^*|^2_{HS}`$; integrate over the circle and apply Parseval. The cross term is at least $`a^2=\sum|M_k|^2`$; the diagonals are bounded by testing the functional on the two ordered products FG and GF (so no commutation is needed), with the Faber weight 2 giving $`\le4a^2/\gamma^2`$. Hence $`2a^2\le8a^2/\gamma^2`$ and $`\gamma \le 2`$ when $`a>0`$. If $`a=0`$, the cross functional vanishes, so its value on $`F`$ gives $`\gamma=0`$. The bounded-operator conclusion is obtained through finite compressions and approximation, without assuming a norm-attaining vector in infinite dimension. This replaces Crouzeix–Palencia’s operator-norm triangle inequality ($`1+\sqrt{2}`$) and Lorist–Schwenninger’s perturbation lemma, whose commutation hypothesis “is not available after matrix amplification”. Combination leaning new: extremal pairs and the positive double layer are known; measuring the compressed block in boundary $`L^{2}`$(Hilbert–Schmidt) had no precedent in the literature examined.

# Four-effect coherence control for two-sided PPT images

[Family 272](../families/openai-math-272.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000082.md) · [Batch B002](../../batches/B002/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let $\omega$ be a density matrix on $\mathbb C^p\otimes\mathbb C^q$ of the form

$$\omega=(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)(\chi\chi^*),$$

where $\chi\in\mathbb C^r\otimes\mathbb C^s$, and $\mathcal L$, $\mathcal L\circ T_r$, $\mathcal M$, and $\mathcal M\circ T_s$ are completely positive. Neither $\chi$ nor the maps must be normalized; $T_r,T_s$ denote matrix transposition in fixed bases. For arbitrary positive local matrices $X_0,X_1,Y_0,Y_1$, set $D_{ij}=X_i\otimes Y_j$ and $p_{ij}=\operatorname{Tr}(D_{ij}\omega)$. The extracted inequality is

$$\|\sqrt{D_{00}}\,\omega\sqrt{D_{11}}\|_1
\le\sqrt{p_{00}p_{01}}+\sqrt{p_{10}p_{11}}+2\sqrt{p_{01}p_{10}}.$$

The local matrices need not sum to the identity. To obtain the estimate, pull them back through the adjoint maps, normalize the two Alice-side effects on the support of their sum, and split the input at the spectral comparison of the resulting commuting effects. Complete positivity gives a direct block estimate; complete positivity after transposition of **both** input factors gives a reversed estimate. Applying the two estimates to the four terms of the split vector proves the displayed bound.

## Role in the source argument

At each complete public transcript, the coherence norm becomes the root fidelity between two conditional states held by Eve. The absence of pointwise POVM normalization is essential for integrating transcript densities. Tensor closure permits joint local processing of arbitrarily many input copies.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [def:represented-class](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Entanglement-with-zero-distillable-secret-key-in-local-dimension-ten-September-27-2026/build/source/sections/foundations.tex#L140)
- [lem:coherence](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Entanglement-with-zero-distillable-secret-key-in-local-dimension-ten-September-27-2026/build/source/sections/coherence.tex#L57)
- [thm:zero-key](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Entanglement-with-zero-distillable-secret-key-in-local-dimension-ten-September-27-2026/build/source/sections/secret-key.tex#L121)

## Antecedents and comparison

Private-state methods already connect off-diagonal trace norms with conditional-state fidelity: see [Horodecki et al., Secure key from bound entanglement](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0309110v2). The [2018 study of key-undistillable states](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.08938v4) is a close problem-level antecedent. The specific four-effect estimate is the candidate extracted device; the broader relation between entanglement and secrecy is established background. This is a targeted comparison, not an exhaustive novelty determination.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the support normalization, the need for a global input transpose in the reversed bound, and the four-term triangle inequality against the source proof.

The represented class is a hypothesis and must not be replaced by all PPT states. The operational 1/5 unhalved trace-norm gap additionally uses the source protocol and transcript theorems; it is not a consequence of positivity alone. The corresponding conventional trace distance is 1/10.

## Possible applications

Potential use: an obstruction to coherent equal-label branches in a two-sided channel construction. Any extension to a different protocol model requires a compatible transcript representation.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Symmetric and exterior squares turn rank loss into a product-free Choi range

[Family 272](../families/openai-math-272.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000082.md) · [Batch B002](../../batches/B002/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let $L:M_4(\mathbb C)\to M_4(\mathbb C)$ be completely positive and PPT, meaning that its output transpose is also completely positive. Suppose twenty distinct projective directions $[x]$ satisfy $\operatorname{rank}L(xx^*)<4$, every nonzero homogeneous quadratic vanishes on at most nine of them, and $L(yy^*)$ is positive definite for some $y$.

Let $U:\mathbb C^{10}\to\operatorname{Sym}^2\mathbb C^4$ and $V:\mathbb C^6\to\bigwedge^2\mathbb C^4$ be the standard isometric embeddings into $\mathbb C^4\otimes\mathbb C^4$. Write $\widehat x=U^*(x\otimes x)$ and let $K$ be the signed complementary-pair map on exterior two-vectors. Define

$$S(A)=V^*(L\otimes L)(UAU^*)V,\qquad R(A)=KS(A)^T K^*.$$

For the real coordinate inclusion $E:\mathbb C^6\to\mathbb C^{10}$, set $\Phi_1(A)=ES(A^T)E^*$ and $\Phi_2(B)=R^*(E^*BE)$, where $R^*$ denotes the Hilbert--Schmidt adjoint. These are PPT maps. Their composite has a nonzero positive Choi matrix $Z$ whose range contains no nonzero product vector.

The mechanism is explicit: rank loss puts $\widehat x\otimes\widehat x$ in $\ker Z$ because $\bigwedge^4\operatorname{ran}L(xx^*)=0$. A product vector in $\operatorname{ran}Z$ would force two nonzero quadratics to have zero sets covering all twenty directions, contrary to $9+9<20$. The positive definite output guarantees $Z\ne0$.

## Role in the source argument

Converts a rank-loss certificate for a small PPT map into nonseparability of a composition on a larger matrix algebra. The source then supplies a separate integer-pencil certificate for the twenty directions.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:tensor-criterion](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Entanglement-with-zero-distillable-secret-key-in-local-dimension-ten-September-27-2026/build/source/sections/geometry.tex#L13)
- [eq:SR](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Entanglement-with-zero-distillable-secret-key-in-local-dimension-ten-September-27-2026/build/source/sections/geometry.tex#L90)
- [eq:kernel-vectors](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Entanglement-with-zero-distillable-secret-key-in-local-dimension-ten-September-27-2026/build/source/sections/geometry.tex#L191)

## Antecedents and comparison

The product-exclusion argument builds on [Bennett et al., Unextendible Product Bases and Bound Entanglement](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9808030v2), [Pittenger](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0208028v1), and [Parthasarathy](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0405077v1). Exterior complementary-pair duality is also established. The candidate contribution is their assembly with a PPT rank-loss map, not the product-exclusion principle by itself. Targeted searches for the PPT/Veronese/twenty-direction combination did not identify an independent earlier instance.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the 10- and 6-dimensional tensor spaces, the Choi input-transpose cancellation, the conjugation required for exterior orthogonality over complex subspaces, and the zero-set counting step.

This is a conditional construction until the hypotheses on L are supplied. The arithmetic certificate was not rerun in this batch. Product-free range is asserted for the dimension-ten composite Choi matrix; it does not persist for every larger flagged completion.

## Possible applications

Potential use: search for other PPT maps with controlled projective rank-loss sets, or replace quadratic evaluation by another explicitly verified interpolation condition.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A two-block switch with an absorbing flag preserves an entangled Choi corner

[Family 272](../families/openai-math-272.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000082.md) · [Batch B002](../../batches/B002/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For any two PPT maps $\Psi_1,\Psi_2:M_m\to M_m$, define $A_i=\Psi_i^*(I)$, $c_i=(1+\operatorname{Tr}A_i)^{-1}$ and $F_i=I-c_iA_i$. On $\mathbb C^m_0\oplus\mathbb C^m_1\oplus\mathbb C e_\star$, let $W_0,W_1$ be the real coordinate inclusions and $P_\star=e_\star e_\star^*$. For diagonal input blocks $X_{00},X_{11},x_\star$, define

$$\Theta(X)=c_2W_0\Psi_2(X_{11})W_0^*
+c_1W_1\Psi_1(X_{00})W_1^*
+[\operatorname{Tr}(F_1X_{00})+\operatorname{Tr}(F_2X_{11})+x_\star]P_\star.$$

Off-diagonal input blocks are discarded. Since $F_i\ge c_iI>0$, this is a trace-preserving PPT channel on dimension $2m+1$. Its flag is absorbing, and

$$(W_0^*\otimes W_0^*)J(\Theta^2)(W_0\otimes W_0)
=c_1c_2J(\Psi_2\circ\Psi_1).$$

Thus a nonseparable composite Choi matrix gives a channel whose square is not entanglement breaking. The original maps need not preserve trace.

## Role in the source argument

Transfers the source dimension-ten PPT-pair construction to a genuine trace-preserving channel in dimension 21.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:channel-completion](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Entanglement-with-zero-distillable-secret-key-in-local-dimension-ten-September-27-2026/build/source/sections/applications.tex#L39)
- [eq:channel](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Entanglement-with-zero-distillable-secret-key-in-local-dimension-ten-September-27-2026/build/source/sections/applications.tex#L78)
- [eq:square-corner](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Entanglement-with-zero-distillable-secret-key-in-local-dimension-ten-September-27-2026/build/source/sections/applications.tex#L119)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source explicitly credits the two-block switch to [Christandl, Müller-Hermes and Wolf, Section IV.A](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.01266v2), and the trace-preserving flag extension to [Filippov, Proposition 3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.05686v3). This card records a reusable combination with an exact corner identity; it does not claim invention of either component.

## Checks and limitations

Checked positivity of the missing-trace effects, trace preservation, the absorbing flag, and the two-step compression identity.

The full Choi matrix has a product summand from the flag. The conclusion is nonseparability of the full matrix, witnessed by a local corner, not a product-free range for the full matrix. The displayed Choi compression uses real coordinate inclusions.

## Possible applications

Potential use: turn non-trace-preserving map-composition examples into physical channels while retaining a specified entangled submatrix.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Four diagonal-form comparisons interpolate to a thermal hyperbolic weight

[Family 273](../families/openai-math-273.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000083.md) · [Batch B002](../../batches/B002/README.md)

## Mathematical content

On coordinate Hilbert spaces $\mathcal H_j$, $0\le j\le k$, define $Q_{X,j}(Z)=\sum_\alpha X_j(\alpha)|Z_\alpha|^2$. Let $\mathcal T\subset\mathcal H_0$ be linear, $L_i:\mathcal T\to\mathcal H_i$ linear, and $w_i>0$. A weight family satisfies comparison when

$$Q_{X,0}(Z)\ge\sum_{i=1}^k w_iQ_{X,i}(L_iZ)\quad(Z\in\mathcal T).$$

At each coordinate let $m>0$ and $x,y\in\mathbb R$, and put $f(x)=x/\sinh x$, with $f(0)=1$. Assume every source test has finitely many parameter values $(m,x,y)$ in its support, and $\mathcal T$ is invariant under scalar functions of that tuple. If comparison holds for all four weights $mf(x)e^{\pm x}$ and $mf(y)e^{\pm y}$, it holds for

$$F=m\frac{f(x)f(y)}{f(x+y)}.$$

No commutation between $L_i$ and the multipliers is assumed. Finite parameter support allows infinitely many nonzero coordinates with the same parameters.

The additional scalar function is defined by $B(f(x)^2)=x\coth x$ for $x\ge0$. The source proves that $-B'$ has a positive Stieltjes representation. For $s=f(x)^2,t=f(y)^2$, this constructs the comparison-preserving weight $E=m(t-s)/(2(B(s)-B(t)))$, with $E=-m/(2B'(s))$ at $s=t$. A quadratic minimization in an auxiliary coordinate then gives exactly $F$.

## Role in the source argument

Combines the variance and entropy-Hessian comparisons at regularized minimizers into the metric used for a thermal-balance defect. It is a standalone comparison theorem, distinct from the full bosonic entropy inequality.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [thm:interpolation](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-entropy-photon-number-inequality-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-interpolation.tex#L32)
- [int:stieltjes](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-entropy-photon-number-inequality-September-24-2026/build/sections/02-interpolation.tex#L149)

## Antecedents and comparison

Parallel sums and positive operator means are classical: [Anderson--Duffin](https://doi.org/10.1016/0022-247X(69)90200-5) and [Kubo--Ando](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01371042). [Guha--Erkmen--Shapiro](https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.5666v2) supplies the EPnI problem, not this interpolation formula. Targeted searches for the four-weight and Stieltjes/EPnI formulations found no independent earlier match; this limited search does not establish priority. The source-specific Stieltjes function and exact target weight are the candidate new combination.

## Checks and limitations

Read the parallel-sum variational argument and scalar minimization, including x=y, x=-y and x=y=0. The numerical checks bundled with this batch compare the independent minimization and target formulas on a finite grid.

The finite-parameter and multiplier-invariance hypotheses are essential to the stated proof. Numerical agreement does not prove the Stieltjes representation or its unbounded-form extension. The source Hessian bound is asserted at its minimizers, not for every quantum channel and state.

## Possible applications

Potential use: transfer several elementary diagonal metric inequalities to a sharper thermal metric when the source test space satisfies the stated invariance conditions.

# Fourth-moment Gibbs regularization supplies seventh-moment control

[Family 273](../families/openai-math-273.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000083.md) · [Batch B002](../../batches/B002/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let $N$ be the total number operator on a finite positive number of bosonic modes and $W=I+N$. For $k>0$ and bounded $B\ge0$, the form

$$K=kW^4+W^{1/2}BW^{1/2},\qquad\mathcal D(K^{1/2})=\mathcal D(W^2),$$

defines a positive self-adjoint operator with compact inverse. Its normalized Gibbs state $\omega=e^{-K}/\operatorname{Tr}e^{-K}$ is faithful, satisfies $\operatorname{Tr}\omega W^7<\infty$, and uniquely minimizes $\operatorname{Tr}\sigma K-S(\sigma)$ over states with finite fourth moment.

The proof writes $K^{-1}=W^{-2}(kI+W^{-3/2}BW^{-3/2})^{-1}W^{-2}$. For an eigenvector $\psi_j$ with eigenvalue $u_j$ of $K$, the weak eigenvalue equation yields

$$kW^{7/2}\psi_j=u_jW^{-1/2}\psi_j-BW^{1/2}\psi_j.$$

The right side is square summable. Polynomial eigenvalue counting for a finite-mode number operator, followed by the factor $e^{-u_j}$, gives the seventh moment.

## Role in the source argument

Justifies logarithmic and unbounded-generator pairings after a fourth-moment penalty is added to the entropy optimization. The source also adds a thermal port, output thermal replacement and relative-entropy penalty; only the fourth-moment coefficient is sent to zero in the final compactness step.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:gibbs-regularity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-entropy-photon-number-inequality-September-24-2026/build/sections/03-minimization.tex#L109)
- [eq:functional](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-entropy-photon-number-inequality-September-24-2026/build/sections/03-minimization.tex#L44)

## Antecedents and comparison

Closed positive forms, compact resolvents, Gibbs minimization and thermal entropy methods are established ingredients. [Beigi--Rahimi-Keshari](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09572v2) gives a prior one-mode variational route to Gaussian optimizers. The extracted feature here is the particular W^4/W^7 regularity package and its role in the multimode argument. No independent novelty claim is made for this auxiliary lemma.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the inverse factorization, the domain used in the eigenvalue equation, and the exponent 7 arising from the W^(7/2) norm.

Bounds may depend on k and B and need not be uniform as the regularization vanishes. A finite-mode number operator and bounded positive B are hypotheses. The lemma alone does not establish attainment or stationarity of the full two-input entropy functional.

## Possible applications

Potential use: regularize a bosonic variational problem so that subsequent traces against low-degree creation and annihilation expressions are defined.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A thermal block decomposition preserves the scalar entropy term

[Family 276](../families/openai-math-276.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000084.md) · [Batch B002](../../batches/B002/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let $X,Y$ have the same finite rectangular shape and satisfy $\operatorname{Tr}XX^*=\operatorname{Tr}YY^*=1$. Let $\alpha,\beta,\eta,\delta\ge0$ sum to one and satisfy $\alpha\delta-\beta\eta=K^2$ with $K\ge0$. Put

$$T=\begin{pmatrix}\alpha XX^*+\beta YY^*&KXY^*\\KYX^*&\eta XX^*+\delta YY^*\end{pmatrix},\quad U_0=\alpha+\beta,\quad U_1=\eta+\delta,\quad u=U_0U_1-K^2.$$

Writing $h$ for binary entropy in nats and $g(u)=h((1+\sqrt{1-4u})/2)$, the source proves

$$S(T)\ge(\alpha+\eta)S(XX^*)+(\beta+\delta)S(YY^*)+g(u),\qquad 0\le u\le\tfrac14.$$

For $u>0$, the coefficient relation is the line $U_1\beta+U_0\eta=u$. Its endpoints are

$$ (\alpha_1,\beta_1,\eta_1,\delta_1)=(K^2/U_1,u/U_1,0,U_1),$$
$$ (\alpha_2,\beta_2,\eta_2,\delta_2)=(U_0,0,u/U_0,K^2/U_0),$$

with weights $w_1=\beta U_1/u$ and $w_2=\eta U_0/u$. Both endpoint matrices factor through a two-by-two block matrix with one zero block, and both have the same scalar term $g(u)$. Entropy concavity therefore preserves that term in the mixture. The source separately handles $u=0$. Equality holds when $X=Y$.

## Role in the source argument

Extends the triangular block inequality to simultaneous thermal excitation and damping, without requiring a pure channel output.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [thm:thermal](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Classical-capacity-and-entropy-inequalities-for-generalized-amplitude-damping-September-24-2026/build/sections/thermal.tex#L25)
- [eq:thermal-table](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Classical-capacity-and-entropy-inequalities-for-generalized-amplitude-damping-September-24-2026/build/sections/thermal.tex#L64)
- [eq:thermal-factors](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Classical-capacity-and-entropy-inequalities-for-generalized-amplitude-damping-September-24-2026/build/sections/thermal.tex#L84)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Tang, Zhu, Bai and Wang](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28592v1) is the source explicitly cited for the zero-block theorem and ordinary-damping additivity. [Fang](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14621v1) studies a converse for the generalized channel. The scalar one-use optimization has older antecedents. The candidate device here is the common-scalar endpoint decomposition; neither triangular entropy nor the binary optimizer is attributed to this extraction. A targeted phrase search found no independent prior instance of that decomposition.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the line equation, both weights, all coefficient recoveries and equality for X=Y. The bundled checks use exact rational coefficient samples and finite-dimensional noncommuting complex Gram matrices.

The determinant relation is a hypothesis; arbitrary four-coefficient block states are not covered. The equality case and finite numerical checks do not prove the general entropy inequality. Its analytic dependency is the triangular block theorem.

## Possible applications

Potential use: extend a zero-pattern matrix inequality along a coefficient segment when every endpoint has the same scalar contribution.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Common Kraus columns retain conditional partner entropy

[Family 276](../families/openai-math-276.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000084.md) · [Batch B002](../../batches/B002/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For $\gamma,\nu\in[0,1]$, define generalized amplitude damping by

$$\mathcal A_{\gamma,\nu}\begin{pmatrix}1-p&z\\\bar z&p\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1-t&\sqrt{1-\gamma}z\\\sqrt{1-\gamma}\bar z&t\end{pmatrix},\qquad t=(1-\gamma)p+\gamma\nu.$$

Set $v(p)=\gamma\nu(1-\nu)+\gamma(1-\gamma)(p-\nu)^2$ and $e(p)=h((1+\sqrt{1-4v(p)})/2)$ in nats. For every finite-dimensional CPTP partner $\mathcal N$ and pure input

$$\psi=\sqrt{1-p}|0\rangle\psi_0+\sqrt p|1\rangle\psi_1,$$

with unit branch vectors that need not be orthogonal, the source's branch bound is

$$S((\mathcal A_{\gamma,\nu}\otimes\mathcal N)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|))\ge e(p)+(1-p)S(\mathcal N(|\psi_0\rangle\langle\psi_0|))+pS(\mathcal N(|\psi_1\rangle\langle\psi_1|)).$$

If $V_\ell$ are Kraus operators of $\mathcal N$, the rectangular matrices with columns $V_\ell\psi_0$ and $V_\ell\psi_1$ retain all three operators $XX^*$, $YY^*$ and $XY^*$. This is the substitution into the thermal block inequality. The function $e$ is convex; recursion and entropy concavity give $S(\mathcal A_{\gamma,\nu}^{\otimes n}(\rho))\ge\sum_j e(p_j)$ for arbitrary mixed input $\rho$ with local populations $p_j$.

## Role in the source argument

Keeps the conditional partner output terms needed to bound an entire Holevo ensemble. Their weighted mean equals the partner marginal of the mean output; an unconstrained minimum-output bound alone would lose this information.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:partner-branch](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Classical-capacity-and-entropy-inequalities-for-generalized-amplitude-damping-September-24-2026/build/sections/output.tex#L84)
- [eq:partner-grams](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Classical-capacity-and-entropy-inequalities-for-generalized-amplitude-damping-September-24-2026/build/sections/output.tex#L120)
- [cor:mixed-bound](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Classical-capacity-and-entropy-inequalities-for-generalized-amplitude-damping-September-24-2026/build/sections/output.tex#L219)
- [eq:partner-marginal](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Classical-capacity-and-entropy-inequalities-for-generalized-amplitude-damping-September-24-2026/build/sections/partners.tex#L34)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Tang et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28592v1) is a close antecedent for ordinary damping and pure-output channels. The source extends the branch argument through its thermal block inequality. Existing single-use optimizer formulas do not by themselves rule out entangled input advantages. This card records the thermal branch mechanism, with novelty provisional and relative to the sources compared.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the common-column identity for the cross operator, the determinant relation after channel substitution, and the population averaging used in recursion. No orthogonality of the branch vectors is used.

The channel and partner are finite dimensional. The stronger arbitrary-partner conclusion is stated in the manuscript but not in its selected Comparator challenge. Collective decoding is allowed; the product input ensemble does not imply optimal separate measurements.

## Possible applications

Potential use: retain an auxiliary channel or system in an entropy estimate instead of discarding its branch information before optimizing an ensemble.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A tested-set conditioning budget gives an explicit threshold exponent

[Family 277](../families/openai-math-277.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000085.md) · [Batch B002](../../batches/B002/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let $G$ be a finite two-player game with entangled value $v<1$ and answer-alphabet product $d\ge1$. For a joint finite-dimensional strategy on $k$ repetitions, write $I_i$ for its binary wins, $W=\sum_iI_i$, $E_C=\{I_i=1\text{ for }i\in C\}$ and $p_C=\Pr(E_C)$. Fix $0<\delta<1-v$ and $0<T\le\delta/4$.

Assume, uniformly over every repetition length, strategy and proper tested set with $p_C>0$, that

$$\tau(C):=\frac{\log(1/p_C)+|C|\log d}{k-|C|}\le T
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\frac1{k-|C|}\sum_{i\notin C}\Pr(I_i=1\mid E_C)\le v+\delta/4.$$

Then, with natural logarithms,

$$\Pr[W\ge\lceil(v+\delta)k\rceil]\le\exp\!\left(-\frac{\delta T}{16(1+\log d)}k\right)$$

for every $k\ge1$, and for the supremum over finite-dimensional strategies. No attainment of the entangled value is needed.

The sampling step draws indices with replacement, so it makes no independence assumption on the indicators. A large upper tail supplies a short fixed tested set of sufficiently large probability whose conditional remaining win rate is too high. Independent tensor copies remove the lower bound on k without changing the exponent. A conditioning error $B\tau^{1/4}$ permits $T=(\delta/(4B))^4$ and hence a fifth-power threshold exponent.

## Role in the source argument

Separates a probabilistic threshold conversion from the analytic conditioning estimate, allowing improved conditioning bounds to be reused without repeating the sampling argument.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:tail-sampling](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Threshold-parallel-repetition-for-finite-dimensional-entangled-games-September-25-2026/build/sections/04-threshold.tex#L42)
- [prop:conditioning-to-tail](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Threshold-parallel-repetition-for-finite-dimensional-entangled-games-September-25-2026/build/sections/04-threshold.tex#L83)
- [prop:song-conditioning](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Threshold-parallel-repetition-for-finite-dimensional-entangled-games-September-25-2026/build/sections/04-threshold.tex#L195)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Rao, Section 8](https://homes.cs.washington.edu/~anuprao/pubs/parrep.pdf) already converts tested-coordinate control into classical concentration; [Yuen](https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.04340v1) uses sampling with replacement; [Bavarian--Vidick--Yuen](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.07466) proves threshold amplification for anchored games. [Song, TR26-199](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/199/) supplies the conditioning input used here. The card isolates the explicit budget-to-rate formula and all-length step; it does not attribute tested-coordinate sampling itself as new.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the fixed-set selection argument, the constants in c/r and c(1+R/r), the proper-subset condition at large k, and N ceil(qk) >= ceil(qNk) in the tensor-copy step.

The conditioning hypothesis must hold uniformly for all lengths and all admitted strategies, not just one fixed strategy. An all-wins theorem is not by itself the required threshold estimate. The supplied Comparator uses delta^13; it is not evidence that the stronger delta^5 statement was kernel-checked in this batch.

## Possible applications

Potential use: convert a different, independently proved conditioning modulus into a threshold concentration rate, while retaining its parameter dependence.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Reference-state rounding on question-support components

[Family 277](../families/openai-math-277.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000085.md) · [Batch B002](../../batches/B002/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a finite question law $\mu$, form the graph on positive-probability pairs $H=\{(x,y):\mu(x,y)>0\}$, joining pairs sharing either local question. Let $H_j$ be its components, $\mu_j=\mu(\cdot\mid H_j)$, and

$$\kappa_\mu=8\max_j\frac{|H_j|-1}{\min_{z\in H_j}\mu_j(z)}.$$

A singleton contributes zero. With the tested-set notation of the conditioning transfer, let $m=k-|C|$, $p=\Pr(E_C)>0$, and $\tau=(\log(1/p)+|C|\log d)/m$. The source bounds the conditional remaining success by

$$\frac1m\sum_{i\notin C}\Pr(I_i=1\mid E_C)
\le v+\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/p)}{2m}}+4\sqrt{\kappa_\mu\tau}+2\kappa_\mu\tau.$$

The exposure argument supplies common vectors with Alice-local and Bob-local approximations. Adjacent support pairs share an approximation. A path to a fixed component root, followed by weighted Cauchy--Schwarz, bounds the total squared replacement error by $\kappa_\mu p\tau$. The root vectors define question-independent states for the component games. Relative entropy and Pinsker control the change in component frequencies after conditioning.

Using $T=\delta^2/(1024(1+\kappa_\mu))$ in the transfer yields rate $\delta^3/[16384(1+\kappa_\mu)(1+\log d)]$.

## Role in the source argument

Handles zero entries and disconnected question support without changing the original game. Each player can identify its support component from the local question, so component strategies combine by tensoring near-optimal finite-dimensional strategies.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:root-conditioning](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Threshold-parallel-repetition-for-finite-dimensional-entangled-games-September-25-2026/build/sections/05-root-support.tex#L35)
- [eq:root-path-error](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Threshold-parallel-repetition-for-finite-dimensional-entangled-games-September-25-2026/build/sections/05-root-support.tex#L126)
- [cor:support-threshold](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Threshold-parallel-repetition-for-finite-dimensional-entangled-games-September-25-2026/build/sections/05-root-support.tex#L223)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Dinur--Harsha--Venkat--Yuen](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.08349v2) uses connection graphs in classical multiplayer repetition. [Chailloux--Scarpa, corrected version](https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.7787v3) is a related distribution-dependent entangled repetition result. The source credits its common resolvent purification to the earlier OpenAI report. The candidate combination is the quantum component-root replacement with the explicit threshold constant, not graph paths or Pinsker inequality.

## Checks and limitations

Checked local identifiability of components, the path-length and minimum-mass estimate, and 1/32+1/8+1/512=81/512<1/4 in the final budget choice.

The constant depends on the smallest positive conditional mass in each component and may be large. The full conditioning theorem depends on the preceding exposure lemma. This is a fixed-distribution bound, not a universal cubic rate independent of the question law.

## Possible applications

Potential use: replace input-dependent quantum representatives by one reference per locally identifiable component when adjacent representatives share a controlled local approximation.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A moment-coordinate tensor square decomposition gives summandwise variance control

[Family 091](../families/openai-math-091.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000086.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let the smooth diffeomorphism $x=\nabla\varphi(z)$ send the probability $e^{-\varphi(z)}dz$ to $Z^{-1}e^{-V(x)}dx$, with $\tau=D^2\varphi>0$. For a compactly supported smooth real test $f$, set $M=\tau^{-1}$, $H=D^2V$, $B=\tau D^2f\,\tau$, $W=\delta_\mu B$ and $u=\delta_\mu W$, where $\delta_\mu$ is negative weighted divergence and acts rowwise on matrices. The source obtains

$$\mathbb E u^2\ge\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(MBHB)+\mathbb E W^THW.$$

The key intermediate term is $\operatorname{tr}((D_xW)^2)$, not $\|D_xW\|_F^2$. After the integrations by parts and a constant coordinate normalization at a point, the remaining cubic tensors satisfy

$$2\|S\|^2+4\langle S,J\rangle+\|J\|^2+\langle J,J^{(12)}\rangle
=2\|S+\operatorname{Sym}J\|^2+\tfrac16\|J-J^{(12)}\|^2.$$

Here $S$ is fully symmetric, $J_{ijk}=h_{ia}C_{ajk}$, $h=D^2f$, $C=D^3\varphi$, and $J^{(12)}$ swaps the first two indices. A further matrix-square remainder is nonnegative.

For $n\ge2$, even integer $q\ge2$, $\epsilon>0$, nonzero $p_i$ and positive $h_i$, take $\psi_i(x)=(\langle p_i,x\rangle/h_i)^q$ and $V=\epsilon|x|^2/2+\sum_i\psi_i$. Combining the tensor estimate with density of the even tests gives, for all real $b_i$,

$$\operatorname{Var}_\mu\!\left(\sum_i b_i\psi_i\right)\le\sum_i b_i^2\mathbb E_\mu\psi_i.$$

The $p_i$ need not span: the positive quadratic term ensures integrability.

## Role in the source argument

Two complementary Cauchy–Schwarz estimates use the gradient and Hessian of each homogeneous summand. Their coefficients add to exactly the required budget. Differentiating the log partition function in logarithmic slab widths then gives concavity, followed by the soft-slab and Wulff limits.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:tensor](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-logarithmic-Brunn-Minkowski-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/tensor.tex#L10)
- [eq:tensor-squares](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-logarithmic-Brunn-Minkowski-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/tensor.tex#L208)
- [prop:variance](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-logarithmic-Brunn-Minkowski-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/reduction.tex#L9)
- [eq:dual-bound](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-logarithmic-Brunn-Minkowski-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/variance.tex#L74)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Fathi, Stein kernels and moment maps](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.04699v3) supplies the moment-map Stein-kernel viewpoint. [Kolesnikov–Livshyts–Rotem](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.12099v3) already connect strengthened variance inequalities to local Brunn–Minkowski problems. The source-specific candidate is the separate budget for each slab summand through the displayed tensor remainder; the underlying transport and Bochner methods are established.

## Checks and limitations

The finite check verifies the tensor identity exactly for symmetric rational tensors, including equality and nonsymmetric negative controls. The two Cauchy–Schwarz steps and homogeneity factors were checked from the text.

The finite check does not validate global moment-map regularity, all integrations by parts or the entire volume theorem. The tensor identity alone cannot be applied to an arbitrary vector field: W must have the specified double-divergence origin.

## Possible applications

A candidate route to variance estimates retaining individual convex penalties, and a diagnostic for finding the precise nonsymmetric tensor error that must be paid in other transport arguments.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.
