# Removing affine obstructions from double-divergence tests without a global lower bound

[Family 091](../families/openai-math-091.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000086.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let $\mu$ have a smooth, strictly positive, even probability density on $\mathbb R^n$. Let $\tau$ be smooth, even and symmetric, with $0<\tau(x)\le\Lambda I$. Put $Af=x\cdot\nabla f-\tau:D^2f$. Assume both

$$\mathbb E[hAf]=\mathbb E[\nabla h\cdot\tau\nabla f],\qquad
\mathbb E[(Af)(A-1)f]=\mathbb E\|\tau^{1/2}D^2f\,\tau^{1/2}\|_F^2$$

for compact smooth tests. Then the $L^2(\mu)$ closure of $\{A(A-1)f:f\in C_c^\infty,\ f\text{ even}\}$ is the entire centered even subspace.

The proof first shows that every $L^2$ distributional solution of $A(A-1)g=0$ is affine. Local ellipticity gives smoothness. Cutoff estimates establish $Ag\in L^2$ before splitting $g=(g-Ag)+Ag$ into eigenvalue-zero and eigenvalue-one parts. The first is constant; graph-norm cutoff approximation and the Hessian identity force the second to be linear. Parity and centering then remove both obstructions.

## Role in the source argument

Extends a dual variance inequality from compactly supported double divergences to arbitrary centered even L2 tests. This justifies substituting the unbounded polynomial slab observable into the final dual inequality.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:density](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-logarithmic-Brunn-Minkowski-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/density.tex#L7)
- [eq:density-two-estimates](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-logarithmic-Brunn-Minkowski-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/density.tex#L85)
- [eq:hessian](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-logarithmic-Brunn-Minkowski-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/identities.tex#L106)

## Antecedents and comparison

The operator belongs to the moment-measure diffusion of [Klartag](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.2767v1); the source credits the transport-Hessian identity to [Kolesnikov–Livshyts–Rotem](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.12099v3). Orthogonal-complement density and cutoff methods are standard. The useful formulation here requires only local strict positivity and a global upper matrix bound, with the necessary operator identities stated explicitly.

## Checks and limitations

Read the cutoff estimates, the L2 splitting and the graph-norm approximation in full. The bundled calculation checks the Gaussian Hermite model, where A has eigenvalues k and A(A-1) has eigenvalues k(k-1).

The Gaussian check illustrates the affine kernel; it does not establish density for a general matrix field. Neither parity nor the Hessian identity can be silently omitted. No operator-domain assertion is assumed merely from the formal expression for A.

## Possible applications

A reusable density argument when a weighted second-order operator has an affine kernel, its coefficients may degenerate at infinity, and a compact-test Hessian identity is available.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Weighted relative moments can be separated into simultaneous embedding coordinates

[Family 094](../families/openai-math-094.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000087.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For distinct $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ in a real $L_p$ space, $1<p<\infty$, write $E$ for the pairs, $\delta_{ij}=\|x_i-x_j\|_p$ and

$$V=\{((z_i-z_j)/\delta_{ij})_{ij\in E}:z\in\mathbb R^n\}.$$

Fix $0<\eta<1/3$ and $b,K\ge1$. Suppose that for **every** strictly positive probability vector $\lambda$ on $E$, a random $F\in V$ exists with $\|F\|_\infty\le K$ almost surely and

$$\sum_e\lambda_e\left|\mathbb E|F_e|^p-b\right|\le\eta b.$$

The distribution may depend on $\lambda$, but $b$ and $K$ must not. Then one obtains an embedding into $\ell_p^d$ with distortion at most $((1+3\eta)/(1-3\eta))^{1/p}$ and

$$d\le\left\lceil C\max\{1,K^{2p}/(\eta^2b^2)\}\log(2n)\right\rceil,$$

where $C$ is absolute. Separate the compact convex set of possible moment vectors from the open coordinate box of radius $2\eta b$. A separating functional $a$, normalized in ell_1, is tested with $\lambda_e=3|a_e|/4+1/(4|E|)$, giving the incompatible bounds $2\eta b$ and $4\eta b/3$. One common distribution therefore exists; bounded independent sampling and a union bound add at most another $\eta b$ per coordinate.

## Role in the source argument

Separates the construction of scalar random increments from the simultaneous embedding requirement. Allowing a common moment b larger than one makes an additive moment error small relative to the metric scale.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:weighted](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-dimension-reduction-in-Lp-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L295)
- [eq:sampling-dimension](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-dimension-reduction-in-Lp-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L309)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Eskenazis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.06602) uses Maurey’s empirical method, distance matrices and a change of measure to obtain additive-error dimension reduction for incompressible sets. The source seeks uniform relative control for arbitrary configurations through a weighted test criterion. Convex separation and the concentration step themselves are standard.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the separating-functional argument, positivity of its test weights, the sampling tail exponent and the conversion from pth moments to a common distance scale.

An existential distribution for each pair separately is insufficient. Bounds that depend on the testing probability do not satisfy the hypothesis. This criterion alone provides neither the required distributions nor an efficient algorithm.

## Possible applications

A modular way to assemble metric embeddings from weighted scalar tests, or to identify exactly where a randomized-coordinate construction lacks uniform relative error.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A fixed-point reweighting turns average electrical localization into uniform row control

[Family 094](../families/openai-math-094.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000087.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Use the normalized-gradient space $V$ above. For each positive pair probability $\lambda$, there is a probability $\sigma\ge\lambda/2$ such that the orthogonal projection $P$ onto $V$ in $\ell_2(\sigma)$ satisfies

$$\|P\|_{\infty\to\infty}=\max_e\sum_f|P_{ef}|\le4\log(2n).$$

Both $P$ and $I-P$ remain contractions in $\ell_2(\sigma)$. To obtain the weights, let $R_e(\sigma)=\sum_f|P_{ef}(\sigma)|$ and $L=2\log n$. The established electrical localization bound implies $\sum_e\sigma_eR_e^2\le L^2$. On $\{\sigma:\sum\sigma=1,\ \sigma\ge\lambda/2\}$ define

$$u_e(\sigma)=\frac{\sigma_eR_e(\sigma)^2}{2L^2},\qquad
\Phi_e(\sigma)=u_e(\sigma)+(1-\sum_fu_f(\sigma))\lambda_e.$$

This is a continuous self-map because $\sum u\le1/2$. At a Brouwer fixed point, $u_e\le\sigma_e$ gives $R_e\le\sqrt2L$, which is the stated bound. The positive lower weights keep the projection’s Gram matrix invertible on the compact domain.

## Role in the source argument

Projects clipped or truncated random increments back onto increments arising from consistent point labels, controlling both the L2 error and the coordinate magnitude.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:localization](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-dimension-reduction-in-Lp-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L392)
- [lem:projection](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-dimension-reduction-in-Lp-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L410)
- [eq:average-row-sums](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-dimension-reduction-in-Lp-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L433)

## Antecedents and comparison

The logarithmic bound for the entrywise absolute transfer-current matrix is the theorem of [Gurel-Gurevich, Nachmias and Sachdeva](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24130v1). This card extracts the subsequent weight selection, not that established localization theorem as a new discovery. Brouwer reweighting is an established general technique; priority for this particular projection formulation is unresolved.

## Checks and limitations

The proof of the self-map and its row estimate was checked. Finite complete-graph examples verify the conjugation to a Euclidean projection, the weighted average row identity and the fixed-point inequalities at numerical solutions.

Numerical fixed-point iteration is only a check on examples: Brouwer’s theorem does not imply convergence of the naive iteration. The bound concerns this graph-gradient projection and does not hold automatically for arbitrary subspaces.

## Possible applications

A template for turning an averaged matrix bound into simultaneous row bounds while preserving a prescribed fraction of every original test weight.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Antipodal row and column incidences force quadratic exact coordinate dimension

[Family 094](../families/openai-math-094.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000087.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix $1<p<\infty$, $p\ne2$, and integer $k\ge2$. In $\ell_p^{k^2}$ let $r_i$ and $c_j$ be the indicator vectors of the rows and columns of a $k\times k$ grid. The $4k+1$ points

$$\{0\}\cup\{r_i,-r_i:1\le i\le k\}\cup\{c_j,-c_j:1\le j\le k\}$$

require at least $k^2$ coordinates in any isometric ell_p embedding, even an unrestricted nonlinear one. Translate and rescale a distortion-one map to fix zero. Strict convexity forces preservation of antipodes. The p-parallelogram defect

$$\|u+v\|_p^p+\|u-v\|_p^p-2\|u\|_p^p-2\|v\|_p^p$$

vanishes exactly when the supports are disjoint: every nonzero scalar defect has the sign of $p-2$. The images of different rows therefore have disjoint supports, as do different columns. Every row–column pair has defect $2^p-4\ne0$, so their image supports intersect. A coordinate can witness at most one of the $k^2$ incidences. For arbitrary $n\ge9$, padding gives the lower bound $\lfloor(n-1)/4\rfloor^2$.

## Role in the source argument

Explains the discontinuity between exact coordinate realization and the source’s approximate dimension reduction, including even integer exponents greater than two.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:disjointness](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-dimension-reduction-in-Lp-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L1079)
- [eq:antipodes](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-dimension-reduction-in-Lp-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L1099)
- [eq:exact-bounds](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-dimension-reduction-in-Lp-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L92)

## Antecedents and comparison

The support test is classical: [Lamperti, Corollary 2.1](https://msp.org/pjm/1958/8-3/pjm-v8-n3-p09-s.pdf). The source credits Ball’s earlier quadratic-order sharpness for 1<=p<2. The candidate extracted device is the finite antipodal incidence configuration extending this argument across p>2; no claim of exhaustive novelty verification is made.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the scalar-sign proof and strict-convexity step. The bundled finite calculation verifies all row/column defects and support incidences for several grid sizes, with p=2 as a negative control.

Exact equality is essential; the proof gives no comparable dimension lower bound at fixed distortion greater than one. Strict convexity excludes p=1 from this argument, and the defect vanishes identically at p=2.

## Possible applications

Encoding combinatorial incidence constraints into exact metric realizations, and constructing small certificates that a proposed coordinate compression cannot preserve all distances.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Separated displacement scales keep unbounded sheet multiplicity uniformly doubling

[Family 098](../families/openai-math-098.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000088.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Take $r_j=1000^{-j}$ and pairs of positive integers $(N_j,W_j)$ in which every pair recurs infinitely often. Above a base point in $\mathbb R^2$, level $j$ permits either zero or $r_je_{j,i}$ in mutually orthogonal directions. Label $i$ is allowed on the union of its periodically colored horizontal strips of width $r_j$ and vertical strips of width $W_jr_j$. Only finitely many levels are nonzero at each point.

Despite unbounded $N_j,W_j$, the resulting Hilbert subset is 76800-doubling. In a ball of radius $t$, levels with $r_j>t$ are fixed. At most one level lies in $(t/64,t]$, where the base projection encounters fewer than 300 labels. The remaining displacement tail has squared diameter at most

$$2\sum_{r_j\le t/64}r_j^2\le\frac{2(t/64)^2}{1-10^{-6}}<(t/32)^2.$$

Partition the base square of side $2t$ into $16^2$ cells of side $t/8$, and group points by cell and intermediate label. Every group has diameter below $\sqrt{33}\,t/32<t/2$. Selecting a center from each nonempty group gives at most $300\cdot16^2$ intrinsic half-radius balls.

## Role in the source argument

Makes room for arbitrarily many recurring branch labels while keeping metric covering complexity uniformly bounded at every radius.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:set](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite-dimensional-bi-Lipschitz-embedding-September-25-2026/build/main.tex#L106)
- [prop:doubling](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite-dimensional-bi-Lipschitz-embedding-September-25-2026/build/main.tex#L115)
- [eq:tail](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite-dimensional-bi-Lipschitz-embedding-September-25-2026/build/main.tex#L124)

## Antecedents and comparison

Multiscale doubling constructions have substantial antecedents, including [Lafforgue–Naor’s Lp obstruction](https://web.math.princeton.edu/~naor/homepage%20files/Lp-doubling.pdf). The particular union of horizontal and vertical permissions is important here because it supplies common sheets at later crossings. The covering argument uses elementary geometric-series and cell counts.

## Checks and limitations

Checked coarse-coordinate rigidity, the single-intermediate-level claim, strip counts and the exact rational tail and diameter bounds. All centers lie in the constructed subset.

This covering estimate alone is no obstruction to finite-dimensional embedding. Recurrence and the shared horizontal/vertical sheet domains are needed by the later derivative argument. The displayed space is not the compact Banach-space example.

## Possible applications

Constructing metric spaces with large combinatorial complexity but bounded local covering counts, provided fine-scale tails and the number of active intermediate labels can both be controlled.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Lexicographic derivative extrema turn crossing sheets into a packing obstruction

[Family 098](../families/openai-math-098.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000088.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Under a proposed bi-Lipschitz embedding of the sheet space into $\mathbb R^k$ with lower constant 1 and upper constant $D$, collect all good-point derivative pairs $(|F_x|^2,|F_y|^2)$ in one compact closure $K\subset[0,D^2]^2$. Let $A$ maximize the first coordinate, and $B$ maximize the second on the first-coordinate face $s=A$. Compactness gives

$$\mathbb E(A-s_n)\to0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\limsup\mathbb E t_n\le B$$

for arbitrary probability-space-valued pairs $(s_n,t_n)\in K$. No quantitative modulus for the second extremum is needed.

Choose fixed $N>(1+2D)^k$ and recurring aspect ratios $W_j=n$. Near $(A,B)$, the source obtains horizontal and vertical selected-sheet errors

$$n^2\langle|G_H^x-F_x|^2\rangle\to0,\qquad
\langle|G_V^y-F_y|^2\rangle\to0.$$

The horizontal estimate has an explicit $O(n^{-2})$ bound after multiplication by $n^2$; the vertical estimate uses only compactness. On one period block of width $Nnr$ and height $Nr$, line selection and Cauchy–Schwarz make normalized offsets vary by at most $\omega_n=N\sqrt{2N\epsilon_n}\to0$. At cross-color intersections two permitted displacements are separated by $\sqrt2r$. Transport along the selected row and column gives $N$ offsets in a radius-D ball, pairwise separated by at least $\sqrt2-2\omega_n>1$. Volume packing contradicts $N>(1+2D)^k$.

## Role in the source argument

Uses a quantitative first-direction estimate to pay for long horizontal lines and a qualitative second-direction estimate for bounded normalized vertical lengths. The same sheet must be used on both arms of each crossing.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:compact](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite-dimensional-bi-Lipschitz-embedding-September-25-2026/build/main.tex#L177)
- [prop:energy](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite-dimensional-bi-Lipschitz-embedding-September-25-2026/build/main.tex#L248)
- [eq:Hrate](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite-dimensional-bi-Lipschitz-embedding-September-25-2026/build/main.tex#L272)
- [eq:omega](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite-dimensional-bi-Lipschitz-embedding-September-25-2026/build/main.tex#L341)

## Antecedents and comparison

Differentiation and separation-versus-stretch arguments precede this source, notably [Laakso](https://doi.org/10.1007/s000390050003). The elementary lexicographic compactness lemma is not presented as a new compactness principle. The candidate instrument is its asymmetric use with recurring crossed sheets and finite-dimensional packing.

## Checks and limitations

Read the two energy estimates and crossing selection in full. Checked the variance expansion, the endpoint errors divided by strip width, the n-scaling and the final packing count.

The compact set K and target parameters must remain fixed as n grows. Independent horizontal and vertical branch maps would not provide the common crossing values. This mechanism is tied to the supplied geometry; it is not a general assertion about all doubling subsets.

## Possible applications

Designing rigidity arguments with several directional energies when only the first direction admits an effective rate, and isolating the geometric compatibility needed for a packing contradiction.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Finite Hilbert obstructions can be assembled into a compact obstruction in any Banach space

[Family 098](../families/openai-math-098.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000088.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose a fixed Hilbert subset S is lambda-doubling and admits no finite-distortion embedding into any finite-dimensional Euclidean space. Compactness of bounded coordinate products implies that for every target dimension and distortion bound there is a finite witness inside S. Choose $X_j\subset S$ excluding distortion at most j into $\mathbb R^j$.

For any infinite-dimensional real Banach space B, Dvoretzky’s theorem places each finite Hilbert span in B with distortion strictly below 2. Translate and shrink the images into finite clusters $C_j\subset B_B(2^{-j}v,2^{-j}/100)$, where v is a fixed unit vector. Then

$$K_B=\{0\}\cup\bigcup_{j\ge1}C_j$$

is compact, has a universal doubling bound $1+6\lambda^8$, and admits no embedding into any finite-dimensional normed space at any finite distortion.

The individual clusters are at most $\lambda^4$-doubling. For a radius-r ball, clusters at scales at most r/4 fit in one tail ball; at most five larger dyadic scales can meet the ball if more than one such cluster does. Each intersection needs at most $\lambda^8$ half-radius balls. An embedding of K_B with Euclidean target dimension k and distortion D contradicts the witness X_j for any j>=k with j>=2D.

## Role in the source argument

Separates the infinite geometric obstruction from compactness and from the ambient Banach space. The initial noncompact sheet construction supplies finite witnesses; classical finite representability performs the transfer.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [cor:banach](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite-dimensional-bi-Lipschitz-embedding-September-25-2026/build/main.tex#L418)
- [sec:banach](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite-dimensional-bi-Lipschitz-embedding-September-25-2026/build/main.tex#L415)

## Antecedents and comparison

Finite-witness compactness and Dvoretzky are classical, not newly proved phenomena. The source explicitly uses only the qualitative finite-dimensional Dvoretzky theorem. Related fixed-set obstructions appear in [Lafforgue–Naor](https://web.math.princeton.edu/~naor/homepage%20files/Lp-doubling.pdf); the present conditional assembly applies to the Hilbert obstruction supplied earlier in the manuscript.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the product-compactness quantifiers, recentering cost in the doubling estimate, dyadic scale count and strict distortion margin. Exact rational checks confirm the tail and cluster-separation constants.

This transfer assumes finite witnesses already exist and gives a very large, nonoptimal doubling constant. It uses completeness of the ambient Banach space through the stated setting and finite-dimensional near-Euclidean representability; no single universal subset is asserted to be isometric in all ambient spaces.

## Possible applications

Turning families of finite metric obstructions into one compact example, while separating source-space placement from target-space impossibility.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Nonlinear Jacobian compatibility forces a linear symmetric matrix field to commute

[Family 101](../families/openai-math-101.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000089.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let $X_1,\ldots,X_m$ be real symmetric m-by-m matrices, $\sum_rX_r^2=I$, and $A(x)=\sum_rx_rX_r$. Put $t(a)=-\log\Phi(-a)$ and $q=t'$, where $\Phi$ is the standard Gaussian distribution function. If $F\in W^{1,2}_{loc}(\mathbb R^m;\mathbb R^m)$ has weak Jacobian $DF=q(A)$ almost everywhere, then an orthogonal change of input and output makes F a product of signed exponential quantile maps, plus a translation:

$$U^TF(Uy)=(\sigma_i t(\sigma_i y_i))_{i=1}^m+w,\qquad \sigma_i\in\{-1,1\}.$$

The local algebra is especially portable. Jacobian compatibility requires $(\partial_rq(A))e_s=(\partial_sq(A))e_r$. Since $q'(0)\ne0$ and $q''(0)\ne0$, its constant term gives $X_re_s=X_se_r$. The linear term then cancels its common leftmost-A factors and gives $[X_r,X_s]x=0$. Thus all coefficients commute. After simultaneous orthogonal diagonalization and rotating the input as well, coefficient symmetry leaves only the ith diagonal entry of the ith coefficient. The sum-of-squares normalization makes it a sign.

The commutation part of this proof uses only analyticity near zero and nonzero first and second derivatives; this is a consequence of the displayed coefficient argument, not a claim that every such scalar function has the exponential-law conclusion.

## Role in the source argument

Classifies the linear matrix fields obtained when higher-chaos slack vanishes in the entropy argument. Applied to Gaussian input, the specified q gives independent mean-one exponentials up to signs and orthogonal transformation, with covariance I.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:linear-jacobian](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-sharp-entropy-bound-and-the-simplex-inequality-for-isotropic-constants-October-5-2026/build/manuscript/rigidity.tex#L13)

Commutation of weak mixed derivatives, analytic functional calculus and simultaneous diagonalization are standard. The source isolates their short combination for this transport field. [Fradelizi–Marín Sola](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07406) provides the surrounding entropy and isotropic-constant context; it is not evidence that this local lemma is new. Targeted searches did not establish priority for the exact formulation.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the cancellation and the input/output rotation explicitly. Exact finite tensor checks compare the linear compatibility residual with the coefficient commutator, including noncommuting coefficient arrays that satisfy the constant-term symmetry.

Without q''(0) != 0, the argument need not force commutation; for an affine q, Hessian fields from cubic potentials provide noncommuting examples. The sum-of-squares identity is needed for the signed rank-one classification, not for the earlier commutation deduction. This lemma alone does not establish the global entropy inequality.

Equality classification in matrix-valued transport arguments and tests of whether a prescribed nonlinear matrix field can actually be the Jacobian of a map.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# An exponential cone density transfers entropy gaps to isotropic-constant gaps

[Family 101](../families/openai-math-101.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000089.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a full-dimensional convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ with centroid zero, let $\Sigma_K$ be its uniform covariance and define the cone $\mathcal C_K=\{(tx,t):x\in K,t\ge0\}$. The log-concave density

$$f_K(y,t)=\frac{e^{-t}}{n!|K|}\mathbf1_{\mathcal C_K}(y,t)$$

is the law of $(TX,T)$, where X is uniform on K and independently $T\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(n+1,1)$. Consequently

$$h(f_K)=n+1+\log(n!|K|),\qquad
\det\operatorname{Cov}(f_K)=(n+1)^{n+1}(n+2)^n\det\Sigma_K.$$

Thus the entropy-gap inequality $h(f)\ge m+\frac12\log\det\operatorname{Cov}(f)$ in dimension m=n+1 implies, exactly,

$$L_K\le\frac{(n!)^{1/n}}{(n+1)^{(n+1)/(2n)}\sqrt{n+2}},\qquad
L_K^{2n}=\det\Sigma_K/|K|^2.$$

If entropy equality characterizes affine images of independent exponentials, the cone support must be an affine image of the positive orthant. Its unique extreme point forces the translation to vanish; its height-one section is then a simplex. Conversely, the cone over a simplex is a linear image of the orthant and gives equality.

## Role in the source argument

Carries a sharp functional inequality and its equality classification to a sharp geometric bound with the exact dimension shift and factorial constant.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:body-cone-density](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-sharp-entropy-bound-and-the-simplex-inequality-for-isotropic-constants-October-5-2026/build/manuscript/geometry.tex#L26)
- [eq:body-cone-determinant](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-sharp-entropy-bound-and-the-simplex-inequality-for-isotropic-constants-October-5-2026/build/manuscript/geometry.tex#L54)
- [eq:body-cone-section](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-sharp-entropy-bound-and-the-simplex-inequality-for-isotropic-constants-October-5-2026/build/manuscript/geometry.tex#L93)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is an established reduction. The source explicitly credits the cone construction to Fradelizi–Meyer and its entropy reduction to [Fradelizi–Marín Sola](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07406), with moment formulas also attributed to Klartag. Its presence in the new source is useful as a reusable bridge, not as evidence of new priority.

## Checks and limitations

Recomputed the normalization, gamma moments, block covariance and determinant. The finite check verifies the simplex covariance determinant and equality constants in several dimensions, including the interval value L=1/sqrt(12).

The transfer is conditional on the entropy theorem and, for the equality conclusion, on its extremizer classification. Neither follows from these gamma-moment calculations. Covariance must be positive definite, so the body is full-dimensional.

## Possible applications

Converting entropy deficits into geometric extremal bounds and tracking equality through homogeneous cone constructions without losing dimension-dependent constants.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

\left|\sum_{1\le n\le X}\lambda(a_1n+b_1)\lambda(a_2n+b_2)\right|

For every smooth connected projective complex surface with $`p_g=q=0`$, degree is an isomorphism $`CH_0(S)\to\mathbb Z`$ with integral coefficients; hence the full Bloch conjecture for $`p_g=0`$ (general type forces $`q=0`$, $`\kappa<2`$ is Bloch–Kas–Lieberman). # The Mahler conjectures

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000053](../papers/P-000053.md)

- [P-000071](../papers/P-000071.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: original inspection: symmetric Lean coverage only; broader solution modules supplied, unbuilt new identity

For origin-symmetric convex bodies $`K\subset\mathbb R^n`$, the source claims $`|K||K^\circ|\ge4^n/n!`$, with equality for linear images of Hanner polytopes. For general convex bodies, use the Santaló point $`s(K)\in\operatorname{int}K`$ and define
``` math
P(K)=|K|\,|(K-s(K))^\circ|.
```
The general claim is $`P(K)\ge(n+1)^{n+1}/(n!)^2`$, with equality exactly for simplices; for a simplex its Santaló point is its centroid. Thus the equality statement for the polar is made after the indicated centering. In the symmetric case $`s(K)=0`$. The third source claims $`c_G(\operatorname{int}K\times\operatorname{int}K^\circ)=4`$ for origin-symmetric $`K\subset\mathbb R^n`$ and $`n\ge2`$, with embeddings at every capacity strictly below 4. The initial extraction inspected symmetric formalization coverage only. The snapshot also supplies general-Mahler and symmetric-polar solution modules; a `sorry` in a comparator challenge is a statement placeholder, not evidence that the separate solution module is a stub. # Moment-coordinate estimates for logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski

## Source manuscript and claim

[The logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski conjecture](../papers/P-000086.md), by OpenAI, None.

The source claims the logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski inequality for all origin-symmetric convex bodies, with the symmetric Lp and scalar B-property consequences. The extracted mechanisms concern the analytic variance argument.

## Dependencies and antecedents

Moment-measure existence and regularity; moment-map Stein kernels; weighted integration by parts; local elliptic regularity; cutoff approximation and soft-slab limits.

Klartag supplies the moment-Hessian diffusion; Fathi identifies the Stein kernel; Kolesnikov–Livshyts–Rotem develop the related transport-Hessian and strengthened Brascamp–Lieb framework. The instrument cards identify the individual comparisons and their limits.

## Review and formalization scope

Read the reduction, adjoint identities, density proof, tensor proof and variance closure. Checked the tensor symmetrization algebra with exact finite arithmetic and the Gaussian model of the test operator. The moment-map construction and its regularity inputs were not independently reconstructed.

The supplied scope document and LogBrunnMinkowski Comparator quantify over all dimensions n>=1 and full-dimensional origin-symmetric bodies. They target the volume inequality, not separate certified statements of these extracted analytic lemmas. No Lean solution was built.

[Subpolynomial dimension reduction in Lp](../papers/P-000087.md), by OpenAI, September 23, 2026.

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: Lean, 475 files, full statement, PCP theorem reproved new gadget

For every fixed $`\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1/2)`$ there is a fixed alphabet $`\mathbb{F}_2^s`$ and a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT to bipartite Unique Games with translation constraints, value $`\ge 1-\varepsilon`$ on satisfiable and $`\le \delta`$ on unsatisfiable inputs. The formal object fixes alphabet, machine and predicates; $`\varepsilon`$ and $`\delta`$ are independent. The development also formalizes a Dinur-style PCP theorem, Håstad’s 3LIN and the Khot–Minzer–Safra Grassmann expansion theorem from scratch.

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000025: Latent alphabet gadget](../instruments/MI-000025.md)

- [MI-000026: Exact table keys with translation-orbit folding](../instruments/MI-000026.md)

Håstad’s 3LIN gap; KMS Grassmann expansion through BKS’s matrix chart; Khot–Saket folding and list decoding; KMS/DKKMS/Minzer–Zheng smooth advice game; Dinur–Steurer parallel repetition twice; Schwartz–Zippel. Not used: Majority is Stablest, high-dimensional expanders, sum-of-squares.

## Caveats.

The argument does not use other OpenAI manuscripts as inputs. Its reduction exponent and alphabet size are tower-like in $`1/p^*`$, which accounts for compatibility with the Arora–Barak–Steurer subexponential algorithm, although the paper does not discuss this point. The reasoning summary records that UGC arose as a subgoal of a different prompt about the basic SDP threshold.

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: not formalized (companion only) combination

For each degree d there is a finite B(d) bounding the number of limit cycles of every real planar polynomial vector field of degree $`\le d`$: the uniform-boundedness assertion in the second part of Hilbert’s sixteenth problem. The bound is ineffective; Écalle–Ilyashenko individual finiteness is not used as a premise. The manuscript has 160 pages. The companion concerns the classical Liénard system $`\dot x=y-F(x)`$, $`\dot y=-x`$, with $`\deg F\le5`$; it claims at most two isolated periodic orbits. [Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

- [P-000017](../papers/P-000017.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: Lean, 276 files, no explicit graph new

The source constructs arbitrarily large m-vertex graphs with independence number $`\le 2`$ and connected-matching number $`<m/100`$, where every pair of matching edges must have an edge between their endpoint sets. The resulting Hadwiger number is $`h(G)<26m/75+2/3`$, hence $`h(G)<0.347m`$ for sufficiently large $`m`$, while $`\chi\ge\chi_f\ge m/2`$. This would also refute the Reed–Seymour fractional weakening and the Füredi–Gyárfás–Simonyi connected-matching conjecture. Parameters: $`g=10^9+1`$, $`m=2^{1000\cdot g\cdot M_0\cdot n}`$; the Lean extracts m from an eventually-true filter statement.

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000031: The hole relation with tensor certification](../instruments/MI-000031.md)

- [MI-000032: Entropy-minimizing container argument](../instruments/MI-000032.md)

- [MI-000033: Scalar recipe / gradient realization / collision machine](../instruments/MI-000033.md)

Plummer–Stiebitz–Toft $`\alpha \le 2`$ reduction; Cambie’s connected-matching-to-minor count; Kleitman–Winston; Csiszár; Ford–Fulkerson; weak regularity; Laurent–Mourrain flat extension.

## Caveats.

The argument gives neither an explicit graph nor an explicit clique-minor number. Many subsequence/compactness steps are non-quantitative by design (“No exponential rate uniform over all stages is asserted”). Illingworth–Steiner’s separate result of 28 September 2026 disproves the dominating variant [source](../../direction/references.md#src:dominating), which requires a stronger kind of clique-minor model. A counterexample to that variant need not violate Hadwiger’s conjecture itself. Both constructions use graphs with $`\alpha\le2`$. The repository supplies a Lean development for the claim surveyed here, but it was not compiled for this survey.

# Erdős’s reciprocal-sum conjecture

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000050](../papers/P-000050.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: original label: companion only; repository also links a headline development, unbuilt new architecture

The source claims $`r_k(N)\le C_kN\exp(-c_k(\log N)^{\varepsilon_k})`$ for each fixed $`k\ge3`$, with $`c_k,\varepsilon_k>0`$, and hence progressions of every finite length in any set with divergent reciprocal sum. The dyadic deduction is valid: for a $`k`$-progression-free set $`A`$,
``` math
\sum_{n\in A\cap[2^j,2^{j+1})}\frac1n
 \le 2^{-j}r_k(2^{j+1})
 \ll_k \exp(-c'_k j^{\varepsilon_k}),
```
and the last expression is summable in $`j`$. By contrast, $`\sum_{m\ge2}\exp(-(\log m)^c)`$ diverges for $`0<c\le1`$ and converges for $`c>1`$. The original discussion of the weaker Leng–Sah–Sawhney log-log bound must be understood in the former range; divergence is not true for every positive $`c`$. The 198-page source uses the LSS inverse theorem as an external input.

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000037: Triangular polynomial cells with descending precision budgets](../instruments/MI-000037.md)

- [MI-000038: Shift comparison and positive counting](../instruments/MI-000038.md)

- [MI-000039: Relative lifting with additive rank and exact marked projection](../instruments/MI-000039.md)

## Reused.

LSS inverse theorem; Schoen–Sisask almost-periodicity; Kelley–Meka sifting; Green–Tao polynomial orbits; Leng’s equidistribution; Candela–Sisask densification; CRT prime boxes.

## Caveats.

The quantitative upper bound was not verified here. The repository documentation links a development for the reciprocal-sum consequence, beyond the lower-bound companion noted in the initial extraction; that development was not built here. The paper claims an improvement from log log to log for every k at once. The trace’s Part I never closed (“circularity concern unresolved”) and Part II ends in “claimed/asserted”. The argument has a long chain of dependencies. An appendix extends LSS to product groups of dimension $`(2+p)^A`$ with a step-drop lemma uniform in parameter count, which the model itself flagged as delicate.

For a commutative Noetherian regular local ring $`R`$ of dimension $`d`$ and nonzero finitely generated $`R`$-modules $`M,N`$ with $`\ell_R(M\otimes_R N)<\infty`$ and $`\dim_R M+\dim_R N=d`$, the source claims $`\chi^R(M,N)=\sum_{i=0}^d(-1)^i\ell_R(\mathrm{Tor}_i^R(M,N))>0`$, without a restriction on characteristic or ramification. The previously open case was ramified mixed characteristic $`V[[x]]/(p-f)`$, $`p\in\mathfrak m^2`$, which Bhatt–Hochster–Ma still called “the most tantalizing problem that remains”. Load-bearing external inputs (Cai–Lee–Ma–Schwede–Tucker perfectoidization results, Land–Tamme cdh descent for truncating invariants, Ma’s Frobenius vanishing) were compared with their arXiv statements in the initial extraction.

Serre’s reduction to prime pairs via Roberts and Gillet–Soulé vanishing; Cohen–Gabber normalization; Faltings normalized length; CLMST perfectoidization in mixed characteristic and perfection plus Monsky and Roberts in characteristic p; Bhatt–Hochster–Ma’s “only $`H_{0}`$ survives” mechanism via a Koszul-polynomial trick.

## Caveats.

The argument relies on several results from 2022–2026. Further checking should focus on the Verdier-quotient identification $`\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(H)`$ and its base change, spectral sequences on idempotent summands that need not lift to chain maps, and the interaction between ultralimits and ordinary limits. A December 2025 AI-generated note had already asserted the prime-quotient form; the paper treats it as a claim rather than an established theorem. ## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: headline not formalized; companions yes new

The source uses the nonrelativistic fermionic Coulomb Hamiltonian on $`\bigwedge^n L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^2)`$, with two electron spin states and kinetic term $`-\Delta/2`$. The $`M\ge1`$ fixed nuclei have distinct positions $`R_j`$ and real charges $`z_j\ge1`$; $`Z=\sum_{j=1}^M z_j`$ is total nuclear charge. The system’s net charge in electron-charge units is $`Z-n`$, and excess electron number is $`n-Z`$. Nuclear repulsion is omitted as a constant independent of $`n`$. For the ground-energy infima $`E_n`$ (with $`E_0=0`$), strict binding $`E_n<E_{n-1}`$ is claimed to imply $`n\le Z+CM`$, with universal $`C`$; threshold bound states are not excluded. For a neutral atom with one nucleus at the origin and integer $`Z\ge1`$, let $`\rho_{\Psi_Z}`$ be the spin-summed density of any normalized ground state, of total mass $`Z`$. Its outer half-electron radius is
``` math
R(\Psi_Z)=\inf\left\{r\ge0:\int_{|x|>r}\rho_{\Psi_Z}(x)\,dx\le\frac12\right\}.
```
The stated bounds are $`0<c\le R(\Psi_Z)\le C`$ and $`0<c\le I_1(Z):=E_Z(Z-1)-E_Z(Z)\le C`$, uniformly in such $`Z`$. The radius retains a fixed exterior mass, not a fixed fraction of all electrons. The initial extraction lists repository formalizations for two Thomas–Fermi asymptotic companions (607 and 428 files), not an independently checked proof of the main strict-binding assertion.

Lieb’s 1984 bound; Zhislin binding; IMS localization; Lewin’s sector localization; Lieb–Thirring; Lieb–Simon Neumann bracketing and Thomas–Fermi theory; Solovej’s coherent states and exterior screened-potential strategy; Bénilan–Brezis.

## Caveats.

The argument has many quantitative parameters ($`L=10^6`$, exponents 1.01, probabilities $`r^{25}`$, $`r^{40}`$); the full bookkeeping was not checked. The formalization catalogue marks “Partial progress”, review “unchecked”, and omits the radii development from its results list. The literature comparison was limited.

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: not formalized new

Let $`\Lambda`$ be a finite induced square-lattice graph, with local dimension $`q\ge1`$, and let $`H=\sum_Xh_X`$ have one Hermitian term per nonempty support $`X`$, with $`\|h_X\|\le J`$ and support diameter at most $`R`$ in the graph distance of $`\Lambda`$. Assume a unique ground state and a full-system gap $`\Delta>0`$. The source claims $`S(A)\le C(q,R,J,\Delta)|\partial_\Lambda A|`$ for every $`A\subseteq\Lambda`$, where $`\partial_\Lambda A`$ is the set of lattice edges crossing from $`A`$ to its complement within $`\Lambda`$. No gap on restrictions, frustration-freeness or translation invariance is assumed. For the open $`L\times L`$ square grid with bounded on-site and nearest-neighbor interactions, a companion gives a normalized PEPS approximation with vector error at most $`L^{-1}`$ and bond dimension at most $`CL^c`$, with $`C,c`$ depending on $`q,J,\Delta`$. The source constructs a finitely generated torsion-free group $`G_{inj}`$, an injection $`\mathbb{Z}^2\to G`$ and a degree-2 class pairing to 1 with the torus, such that the Bott class dies in $`K_0(C^*_rG)`$: rational injectivity of the reduced, coefficient-free assembly map fails. The claim does not contradict classical Novikov or maximal injectivity (Hanke–Schick). The source asserts finite generation; it establishes neither finite presentation nor its failure. The corrected Antonini–Buss–Engel–Siebenand result concerns specified exotic group $`C^*`$-algebras for finitely presented groups; identifying its target with the reduced algebra needs an additional condition, such as exactness, which is also not supplied here. Companions: a torsion-free group with a projection of trace in $`(0,1/2)`$ (surjectivity failure, Kadison–Kaplansky fails) and a group with p-torsion and an irrational-trace projection.

## Extracted instruments.

$`L(\mathbb{F}_n)\cong L(\mathbb{F}_{n+1})`$ for $`n \ge 3`$ by exhibiting a freely generating Haar n-tuple inside $`L(\mathbb{F}_{n+1})`$; $`L(\mathbb{F}_2)\cong L(\mathbb{F}_3)`$ via Dykema’s amplification at $`t=\sqrt{2}`$; Rădulescu’s dichotomy then makes all interpolated free group factors $`L(\mathbb{F}_r)`$, $`1<r\le\infty`$, isomorphic with fundamental group $`\mathbb{R}_{>0}`$. One consequence is that free entropy dimensions would not be generator invariants. The claim differs from expectations recorded in the initial extraction; Popa 2024 and Schafhauser–Tikuisis–White 2025 list the problem as open.

# Hyperinvariant subspaces and transitive algebras

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000025](../papers/P-000025.md)
- [P-000044](../papers/P-000044.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: Lean, 1,108-module import closure new

On every infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space there is a nonzero bounded quasinilpotent operator S ($`\|S^n\|\le\exp(-10\lfloor(n+1)^2/4\rfloor)`$) with no nontrivial closed hyperinvariant subspace; its commutant is a proper strongly closed transitive algebra, refuting Kadison’s transitive-algebra problem as well, which the catalogue summary omits. Companion: for every irrational rotation, an operator in the hyperfinite $`\mathrm{II}_{1}`$ factor with no nontrivial invariant projection in the factor, answering Zhu–Fang–Shi and the point-mass Brown-measure case left open by Haagerup–Schultz. Nothing is said about the ordinary invariant subspace problem.

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000098: Backward intertwiner over an ergodic base](../instruments/MI-000098.md)

- [MI-000099: Endpoint-conditioned convolution obstruction](../instruments/MI-000099.md)

- [MI-000100: Affiliated transport](../instruments/MI-000100.md)

## Reused.

Domar’s convex-envelope theorems (reproved); Douglas–Pearcy equivalence of the hyperinvariant and transitive-commutant problems; Dykema 2005 on projections of hyperinvariant subspaces; Anantharaman–Popa crossed products; Borel–Cantelli; Fejér kernels.

## Caveats.

The repository provides two formalization routes; neither was compiled or kernel-checked for this survey. The companion’s estimates ($`m^{(7/10)m}`$, $`m^{1000}`$) were not independently verified. Remark 1.5 asserts a published 2017 corollary is false. The companion estimates and comparisons with earlier equivalence claims require further checking.

## Recorded assessment

- Novelty: new
- Formalization: ,108-module closure, two formal routes
- Statement coverage: yes
- Dependencies: mutual elementary lemmas with companion
- Antecedents: —

# Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every dimension

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000057](../papers/P-000057.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: not formalized new

Every locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected Hausdorff second-countable topological manifold of positive finite dimension without boundary is a Lie group. The equivalent exclusion concerns faithful jointly continuous $`\mathbb{Z}_p`$ actions on such manifolds, for every prime $`p`$. Pardon’s 2013 proof covered dimension 3 via Smith theory and geometrization; the surveyed argument does not use Yang’s theorem, Smith theory, cohomological dimension or cell-like maps.

Newman 1931 and Pardon’s chart reduction; Kashiwara–Schapira duality; Balmer’s triangular Witt groups; Woolf’s cone lemma; Ranicki–Weiss cutoff; Hardt triviality; Dranishnikov–Ferry–Weinberger telescope; Čech theory and Haar averaging.

## Caveats.

Several steps require closer examination: whether the Balmer–Walter hypotheses pass to localizations of the generated categories; whether $`Rt_*`$ commutes with the infinite eigensheaf sums used; and whether the restricted pairing is isometric in the germ quotient. The odd stabilization $`d>n`$ is essential to the argument.

# Kervaire invariant at the prime three

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000059](../papers/P-000059.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: not formalized combination claims a new element exists

With $`b_j\in\mathrm{Ext}^{2,4\cdot3^{j+1}}`$, the survivors are exactly $`j\in\{0,2,3\}`$: $`b_1`$ dies (Toda), $`b_j`$ dies for all $`j \ge 4`$, and $`b_3`$ survives, giving an order-three element in $`\pi_{322}S_{(3)}`$. This is a finite survivor list with a missing index $`j=1`$; the odd-primary Adams-family indexing differs from the classical prime-two Kervaire invariant convention. The result would also refute Belmont–Ray’s Conjecture 0.1(3). HHR’s 2011 odd-primary note explicitly left $`\theta_{4}`$ at $`p=3`$ open.

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000104: Finite Euler bound](../instruments/MI-000104.md)

- [MI-000105: Exact cyclic coefficient model and fixed geometry](../instruments/MI-000105.md)

- [MI-000106: Lattice forcing from the known survivor](../instruments/MI-000106.md)

## Reused.

Adams–Novikov spectral sequence; Miller–Ravenel–Wilson 2-line; Toda differentials; Belmont–Ray CM detection via Lubin–Tate; Selick’s criterion; Amelotte’s $`\theta_{3}`$; the positive branch uses a truncated extended-cube construction from the stem-106 element, followed by Moore-spectrum and Adams–Novikov corrections (23,384 unknowns in the finite calculation). This produces stem $`3\cdot108-2=322`$; the ordinary ring cube would lie in stem $`3\cdot106=318`$ and is not the claimed new element.

## Caveats.

The claimed conclusion includes a new stable homotopy class. Its verification requires about 1,700 lines of differential calculations, with several statements specified only “up to nonzero scalar” entering a sign-sensitive character test. Although the paper has a reproducibility section, no code is supplied.

# The complete Crouzeix conjecture

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000016](../papers/P-000016.md)
- [P-000066](../papers/P-000066.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: Lean, all sizes, matrix-valued, arbitrary Hilbert space combination leaning new

For every bounded operator $`A`$ on a nonzero complex Hilbert space, including infinite-dimensional spaces, and every matrix polynomial $`P(z)=\sum_k B_kz^k`$, the stated complete inequality is
``` math
\left\|\sum_k A^k\otimes B_k\right\|
 \le2\sup_{z\in W(A)}\|P(z)\|
 =2\max_{z\in\overline{W(A)}}\|P(z)\|.
```
The constant 2 is sharp. The numerical range need not be closed in infinite dimension, which is why the supremum or its closure is used. The holomorphic extension concerns matrix-valued functions holomorphic on an open neighborhood of $`\overline{W(A)}`$; rational functions must have all their poles outside $`\overline{W(A)}`$. In this sense the closure is a complete 2-spectral set. Scalar proofs are presented in the 2026 preprints of Jin, Lorist–Schwenninger and Luo [source](../../direction/references.md#src:jin) [source](../../direction/references.md#src:lorist) [source](../../direction/references.md#src:luo). Lorist–Schwenninger explicitly explain why their proof and Jin’s do not directly give the completely bounded version.

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000107: Ordered density comparison](../instruments/MI-000107.md)

- [MI-000108: Exterior Faber coefficients and the positive kernel](../instruments/MI-000108.md)

- [MI-000109: Optimal metric and endpoint extremal](../instruments/MI-000109.md)

## Reused.

Delyon–Delyon and Crouzeix–Palencia double-layer positivity; exterior conformal maps and Faber polynomials; Paulsen’s similarity theorem; Stein 1952; Sz.-Nagy dilation; Katsnelson–Kheifets–Yuditskii colligations.

## Caveats.

The structural theorem applies separately to each enclosing domain strictly containing $`\overline{W(A)}`$; no limiting similarity on the closure is asserted. Luo’s scalar argument also uses a top singular pair [source](../../direction/references.md#src:luo), so that ingredient alone is not evidence of novelty. The relation between its boundary certificates and the matrix-valued argument here requires closer comparison.

## Recorded assessment

- Novelty: combination leaning new
- Formalization: files, five challenges
- Statement coverage: yes, full cb statement
- Dependencies: no
- Antecedents: Luo 2026 (novelty comparison incomplete)

# Relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell, 3D, large data

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000041](../papers/P-000041.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: Lean, 207 files, continuation step included combination

For the one-species system with no background charge, the source assumes
``` math
\begin{gathered}
 f_0\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R_x^3\times\mathbb R_v^3),\qquad f_0\ge0,\\
 E_0,B_0\in C_b^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)\cap L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3),\\
 \nabla\cdot E_0=\rho_{f_0},\qquad \nabla\cdot B_0=0,\qquad
 \rho_{f_0}(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f_0(x,v)\,dv.
\end{gathered}
```
Here every spatial derivative of the fields is bounded, the fields have finite energy, and the nonnegative phase-space datum is smooth and compactly supported. Under these hypotheses the paper claims a unique global classical solution, smooth on each finite time interval and with compact phase-space support there, without a size restriction. The repository supplies a formalization covering a continuation statement; it was not compiled or kernel-checked for this survey.

Cheverry–Ibrahim is cited six times in the summary and omitted from the paper. The exponent comparison has a small margin. A repository formalization is supplied, but no machine check was run for this survey. Uniqueness is asserted only among global classical solutions.

# Universal computation in forced Navier–Stokes flows

[Family index](../../tables/families.md) · [Batch B001](../../batches/B001/README.md)

The statements and assessments below report the direction paper’s extraction. They do not certify the source proofs.

## Source manuscripts

- [P-000006](../papers/P-000006.md)
- [P-000029](../papers/P-000029.md)
- [P-000036](../papers/P-000036.md)
- [P-000040](../papers/P-000040.md)
- [P-000043](../papers/P-000043.md)
- [P-000049](../papers/P-000049.md)
- [P-000051](../papers/P-000051.md)
- [P-000076](../papers/P-000076.md)
- [P-000078](../papers/P-000078.md)

## Family description

Source status as recorded in the direction paper: lemmas formalized; main paper not incremental

For each fixed positive computable viscosity $`\nu`$, an effective procedure maps a Turing machine and input to a smooth mean-zero force on $`\mathbb{T}^{3}`$, time-independent for $`t \ge 1`$, such that Navier–Stokes from rest has a global smooth solution and a marked material particle enters a fixed region in finite time iff the machine halts. Variants: $`\mathbb{R}^{3}`$ with compact support, force decaying faster than any power, an Eulerian velocity observer. The family contains nine closely related manuscripts.

## Extracted instruments.

- [MI-000113: Injective local compiler](../instruments/MI-000113.md)

- [MI-000114: Effective parking and routing isotopy](../instruments/MI-000114.md)

- [MI-000115: Scale-nested memories under rapidly vanishing forcing](../instruments/MI-000115.md)

## Reused.

Moore’s generalized shifts and gapped radix coding; Turing’s printing problem; Leray’s energy uniqueness; Helmholtz–Leray projection; heat-kernel bounds.

## Caveats.

For a chosen smooth divergence-free $`U`$ with $`U(0)=0`$, setting $`f=U_t+(U\cdot\nabla)U-\nu\Delta U`$ makes the Navier–Stokes identity hold with zero pressure. This residual construction does not automatically establish the required mean-zero condition, effective description, bounded derivatives, spatial support, eventual stationarity or time decay of the force; the properties prescribed in each version still require proof. Stationary Euler solutions are not generally Beltrami. The cited Cardona–Miranda–Peralta-Salas–Presas construction uses Beltrami fields, a special class of stationary Euler flows, to realize computation. The forced constructions therefore have a different scope from that construction and from unforced or low-mode-controlled flows. Computation is exact-real reachability with no finite-precision tolerance, as the papers concede. No fresh literature search was completed for this entry.

## Recorded assessment

- Novelty: incremental
- Formalization: of 9 manuscripts, engineering lemmas
- Statement coverage: —
- Dependencies: dependencies among nine public manuscripts; main self-contained
- Antecedents: Agrachev–Sarychev (not engaged)

patterns.title: Auxiliary structure manufactured by the proof
patterns.body:
# Auxiliary structure manufactured by the proof

[Pattern index](README.md)

An argument may introduce auxiliary structure with properties it can control, and then prove that the original object is constrained by that structure.

The UGC construction introduces a latent alphabet hidden from the honest player. The proof of $`\mathrm{L}=\mathrm{BPL}`$ uses one shared O(log n)-bit environment for all samplers. In the Mézard–Parisi argument, a finite auxiliary hierarchy is refined only after $`N\to\infty`$. The ionization proof uses a decreasing chain of observation $`\sigma`$-fields. The BSD argument introduces tame Iwasawa variables and specializes them to zero at the end.

patterns.title: Consequences and proposed extensions
patterns.body:
# Consequences and proposed extensions

[Pattern index](README.md)

Some entries describe consequences of the stated results or suggest extensions beyond them. Each requires its own hypotheses and argument. The cards distinguish consequences presented as following from the source from adaptations that still need a proof.

The centers $`(r^j,jp_i/q_i)`$ suggest a possible analogue of the $`\pi`$ argument for $`r\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\setminus\{1\}`$. Establishing $`\mu(\log r)=2`$ would require a separate interpolation, height and determinant argument; it does not follow verbatim from the theorem surveyed here. The claimed free-group-factor isomorphism would refute the Connes–Shlyakhtenko $`L^2`$-Betti conjecture for $`L(\mathbb{F}_n)`$, a consequence not discussed in the paper. In the second group, the hyperinvariant-subspace counterexample would also refute Kadison’s transitive-algebra problem, which the catalogue summary omits; the Mézard–Parisi lower bound is stated for bounded interactions with permutation-invariant law, odd arity included.

patterns.title: Entropy and information as proof devices
patterns.body:
# Entropy and information as proof devices

[Pattern index](README.md)

Mutual information, relative-entropy projections, and entropy inequalities organize estimates in several proofs. The information quantities measure how much dependence or conditioning is available, and incompatible upper and lower bounds produce a contradiction.

The Kakeya proof uses a mutual-information bound to apply a projection theorem to dependent events. The Hadwiger construction combines Kleitman–Winston recording with a Csiszár I-projection as its progress measure and a Ford–Fulkerson cut as its stopping certificate. The matrix-multiplication argument for $`\omega`$ uses an entropy inequality for a shared tensor leg, while the zero-divisor construction bounds repeated traversals of a random graph by entropy. In the second group, conditioning in the ionization argument costs $`\log^5(e/p)`$ times the inverse squared noise scale in energy. The area-law proof expresses conditional mutual information through a log-norm derivative, and the Haldane-gap proof uses a Rényi-2 purity bootstrap.

patterns.title: Established methods in new settings
patterns.body:
# Established methods in new settings

[Pattern index](README.md)

A recurring contribution is the application of an established theorem in a different mathematical setting. The relevant novelty question concerns that application and its surrounding argument; the imported theorem retains its original attribution.

The examples include the Benyamini–Sternfeld theorem of 1983 on Lipschitz maps without approximate fixed points in an amenability argument; Gross’s 2019 conformal Skorokhod map in the Mahler proof; and Kubota–Patterson cubic theta theory from 1977 in a zero-free-region argument. Other transfers use Fox calculus and free Poisson laws for free group factors, Lelong numbers for volume products, and Lipton–Tarjan separators for diagrams of van Kampen type. The second group applies Braverman’s 2009 $`\mathrm{AC}^{0}`$ theorem to Chowla correlations, Marian–Oprea–Pandharipande localization to Bloch’s conjecture, Lion–Rolin preparation to Hilbert’s 16th problem, Ueda’s reduced HNN extensions to Naimark’s problem, Suzuki’s quantum transfer matrix to the Haldane gap, and Kubo–Ando means to the area law.

patterns.title: Estimates become extremal problems
patterns.body:
# Estimates become extremal problems

[Pattern index](README.md)

A proposed inequality can be studied through the regularity of its optimal-exponent function. Assuming that the desired bound fails, differentiation of this function imposes conditions on an extremal configuration. The proof then rules out a configuration satisfying those conditions.

In the three-dimensional Kakeya argument, coordinatewise monotonicity gives local BV regularity and approximate differentiability almost everywhere. An additional monotonicity comparison yields ordinary total differentiability, and the partial derivatives determine the relevant plank shapes. The four-dimensional argument uses a “horizon” defined by an infimum over quadratic fits. In the Erdős argument, a potential controls the loss at each weight using only the higher weights.

patterns.title: Existence instead of construction
patterns.body:
# Existence instead of construction

[Pattern index](README.md)

Several arguments establish existence through compactness, spectral duality, random sampling, or a terminating search whose output has not been computed. The resulting existence statement need not supply an object of practical size.

The proof of $`\omega \le 9/4`$ bounds the asymptotic spectrum without providing a competitive finite matrix size. The Hadwiger argument selects m through an ultrafilter, and the Hilbert 10 reduction uses a nonstandard root. The zero-divisor and direct-finiteness constructions use random choices or searches with parameters such as $`q=2^{217}`$ and $`n\gtrsim e^{300000}`$. In the second group, the Hilbert 16 argument gives an ineffective B(d), the nearby-Lagrangian example has no explicit dimension, and the Borsuk construction supplies a continuous set without extracting a finite subset. These examples differ in effectivity, but each leaves some construction data unspecified or unevaluated.

patterns.title: Label versus content
patterns.body:
# Label versus content

[Pattern index](README.md)

A title may suppress restrictions that are essential to the mathematical statement. The extraction therefore records the precise model, hypotheses, and conclusion, including computational assumptions where they occur.

“Universal computation in Navier–Stokes” uses volume-preserving flows and a force defined by the residual; the prescribed forcing properties, including eventual stationarity, remain mathematical constraints to verify. “Baum–Connes counterexample” is reduced, coefficient-free rational injectivity for a finitely generated group; finite presentation is not determined, and the claim does not refute the classical Novikov conjecture. “Three MUBs in dimension six” rests on a binary64 computation conditional on compiler semantics. “Ionization conjecture” is the strict-binding formulation, with threshold bound states not excluded. “Beyond the square-root exponent” is $`2^{\omega(\sqrt{n})}`$ at inverse-tower rate, not $`2^{n^{1/2+\varepsilon}}`$ for a fixed $`\varepsilon>0`$.

patterns.title: Parity and characters over finite fields
patterns.body:
# Parity and characters over finite fields

[Pattern index](README.md)

Four constructions use cancellation in finite fields, either through a scalar identity or through vanishing character sums.

The direct-finiteness construction requires $`\ell+1=0`$ in K. The zero-divisor construction uses projective lines whose pairwise intersections have odd size. The UGC gadget is defined over $`\mathbb{F}_2^s`$ and contains a quadratic block over $`\mathbb{F}_{2^d}`$. The proof of $`\omega \le 9/4`$ applies a DFT across $`L=5M`$ copies to select exactly the matching labels.

patterns.title: Probability imported into deterministic problems
patterns.body:
# Probability imported into deterministic problems

[Pattern index](README.md)

Several proofs introduce a random or ergodic auxiliary system into a deterministic problem. Almost-sure statements or measure-zero obstructions in that system then support the deterministic conclusion.

In the hyperinvariant-subspace construction, operators are assembled over the 2-adic odometer, where a finite integer-valued measurable label cannot strictly decrease almost everywhere along the measure-preserving dynamics. The ionization argument smooths and conditions electron positions. Marked Poisson perturbations provide the hierarchy in the Mézard–Parisi proof, while the Baum–Connes construction uses a local-lemma probability law along an infinite tower. The plane-coloring argument uses Haar rigidity for the unrestricted laws considered there.

patterns.title: Rediscovery without citation
patterns.body:
# Rediscovery without citation

[Pattern index](README.md)

The initial comparison identified several constructions closely related to earlier work that was not cited in the manuscript. In some cases, the corresponding reasoning summary does name the earlier source. These comparisons matter when distinguishing a new instrument from a reconstruction or adaptation.

The Vlasov–Maxwell manuscript uses a time-integrated momentum increment related to Cheverry–Ibrahim’s work, which is cited six times in the reasoning summary but absent from the paper. The interpolation argument for $`\pi`$ has antecedents in Masser and Fischler–Nakamaye; the spectral argument for $`\omega`$ follows a template in Alman–Li’s 2026 “Strassen calculus”; and the Kakeya comparison identifies Rios–Sawyer as an uncited antecedent. In the second group, the Mézard–Parisi reasoning summary names Mourrat–Panchenko and Barbier–Panchenko, while the paper omits them. The Serre-positivity argument uses an orbit lemma of Suslin–Voevodsky without citation.

patterns.title: Rigidity theorems that erase regularity hypotheses
patterns.body:
# Rigidity theorems that erase regularity hypotheses

[Pattern index](README.md)

Some arguments replace a regularity assumption with a transfer theorem. The theorem connects the unrestricted object to a measurable, constructible, or otherwise controlled formulation, so that the remaining proof can use that formulation.

For plane coloring, the transfer states that a proper coloring exists exactly when a weak measurable coloring exists. The Hilbert–Smith argument uses sheaf categories generated by arbitrary continuous maps from polyhedra while retaining invertible Verdier duality. The Hilbert 10 argument uses an oracle reduction without constructing a definable copy of $`\mathbb{Z}`$.
